t: Blessed to Keep the Law
v: Where there is no revelation, the people cast off restraint; but one who keeps the law is blessed.
b: In this verse God reminds us to keep the law, because only in this way can we receive blessing. The law does not refer only to the commandments of the Bible. It also includes the various standards and guidance God gives us, so that we know how to live rightly. This is God’s love and care for us. He wants to protect us through the law, so that we can stay away from sin and walk in the way of righteousness.

Keeping the law is not an easy thing. Life is full of temptations and difficulties, and we easily stray from the right path and forget God’s teaching. But when we persist in keeping the law, we can receive true blessing. This blessing is not only material abundance and smooth progress, but even more the peace and joy within. God’s law helps us build right values and standards of conduct, so that we find direction and purpose on life’s journey.

In society today, we may sometimes lose our way and not know how to live. We may be troubled by all kinds of temptations and worldly values, and easily slip into indulgence and selfishness. Yet God calls us to keep His law. These laws are guidance for us, letting us know what is right and what is wrong.

There was once a young man named Shicheng who sought pleasure and enjoyment in college and lost his goals and values. One day he met a Bible teacher, who told him: “If you want to find true happiness and peace, you must keep God’s law.”

Shicheng began to listen to God’s word and tried to keep the law. He found that when he kept the law, his life began to change. He no longer pursued fleeting pleasure, but sought lasting joy and peace. He learned to love his neighbor, respect others, and spend each day with a thankful heart.

In the same way, when we keep God’s law, we too will receive blessing. Keeping the law does not mean being overly strict or depriving ourselves of enjoyment. On the contrary, keeping the law is to protect us, so that we can enjoy true freedom and joy.
ah: Receiving revelation and keeping God’s law in daily life is not only an expression of faith, but also one of our core missions as Christians. Here are some concrete and effective methods that can help you practice and follow God’s law:
a: Prayer and silence

Through prayer and moments of focus, build a connection with God and seek His will and revelation. As you wait in silence, God may reveal His heart or give direction. Such moments of silence can help you feel God’s guidance and leading.
Reading and studying the Bible
Study the Bible deeply to understand God’s word and what He asks of us. By studying the Bible, you will understand God’s law better and know how to put it into practice in daily life.
Meditation and application

After reading, take some time to meditate on God’s word and think about how to apply it to your own life. Ask yourself: What does this passage reveal for my life? How should I put these teachings into practice concretely?
Integrating God’s law

God’s law is not only the Ten Commandments; it touches every area of life. Strive to apply God’s law to your thoughts, words and deeds, and interactions with others. For example, be honest in the workplace, show love and compassion to others, keep justice in finances, and so on.
Community and church participation

Study and share together with other Christians, and take part regularly in church gatherings and small group activities. Such interaction and sharing can provide support and encouragement and help you put God’s law into practice in daily life.
Treating others well

God’s law teaches us to love others as ourselves. Bring this lesson into your daily life and develop the habit of caring for others. Over time, such kindness and love will become your natural response. Most important, always remember God’s grace and His love for you. When we sincerely seek to receive revelation and keep God’s law, God’s Holy Spirit will also give us strength and wisdom. Throughout the journey, let us rely on God’s grace and practice these methods with thankful and joyful hearts. May God’s blessing be with you!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find true blessing on the road of keeping the law and become a witness for God. Amen.

t: Blessed to Hear and Keep
v: Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of the prophecy, and keep the things that are written in it, for the time is near.
b: In this verse we see a wonderful promise God gives us: those who hear and keep God’s word are blessed. This is because when we listen to God’s guidance and follow His will, we receive abundant life in His grace.

There was a gardener who tended his garden every day, giving every flower enough sunshine, water, and nutrients, and promptly pruning away the withered parts. Because of the gardener’s care, the flowers grew strong and bloomed beautifully, colorful and giving off an intoxicating fragrance.

This gardener is like our God, and the garden stands for our lives. When we are willing to listen to God’s word and submit to His will, He is like that gardener, giving us the light, nourishment, and pruning we need. When we walk with God, our lives too will grow strong like the flowers in the garden, showing God’s glory and giving off the fragrance of love and joy.

Yet at times we may meet difficulties and trials. Like the flowers in the garden, we too face storms and cold weather. But when we hold fast to our faith and keep relying on God’s word, He will give us strength and courage to face every challenge. And we can believe that those who hear God’s word and keep what is in it are blessed, because the time is near, and God’s promises will be fulfilled in their lives.

So let us work every day to listen to God’s voice and follow His will. Not only hearing, but putting it into action, becoming faithful disciples of God. When we act this way, we can experience God’s blessing and become God’s witnesses in this world.
ah: Hearing God’s word and keeping it is the longing of every Christian. In daily life we can put God’s word into practice and keep it in the following ways.
a: First, build an intimate relationship. To hear God’s word, we need to build an intimate relationship with Him, like talking with a close friend. This means we need to spend time in prayer and Bible reading, and open our hearts to God.

Second, learn to listen. In our busy lives we easily overlook God’s voice. Yet God often communicates with us through various ways and means, such as the Bible, sermons, and serving in ministry. We need to open our hearts, listen attentively, and discern God’s word.

Third, apply God’s word to life. God’s word is the guide of our lives and the foundation of our actions. When we hear God’s word, we should actively think about how to apply it to our lives. This may require changing our attitudes, behavior, or choices to line up with God’s will.

Fourth, seek wisdom and guidance. Sometimes we may be unsure how God’s will applies to a particular situation or decision. In that case, we can pray and ask God for wisdom and guidance. God will answer us in many ways, including the prompting of the Holy Spirit, the advice of others, or a change in circumstances.

Finally, cultivate an attitude of obedience. To keep God’s word, we need a heart of obedience. This means we are willing to put aside our own wishes and plans and submit to God’s will. Obedience is an ongoing process, and we need to remind ourselves constantly and ask for the Holy Spirit’s help.

Putting God’s word into practice in daily life takes perseverance and endurance. Yet when we sincerely long to hear God’s voice and keep His will, God will surely give us guidance and strength. Let us hold on with faith, hope, and love, and see God at work in our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: May you hear God’s voice every day and keep His word. May God’s grace and peace always be with you. Amen.

t: Blessed to Keep the Sabbath
v: Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast; who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.”
b: In modern society we are always busy with work, study, and all kinds of affairs. Time never seems to be enough, and we forget to slow down and build an intimate relationship with God. Yet through this passage God reminds us that it is a blessing to keep the Sabbath.

Keeping the Sabbath is not only stopping work on a particular day. More important, it creates a spiritual Sabbath within our hearts. This means we focus each day on communion with God, and on His word and His will. It is just as Jesus said in Matthew 11:28-30: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.”

In this busy society we often feel weary and pressured. But when we focus on our relationship with God, He gives us strength and comfort. Just as Psalm 23:1-2 says: “Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.”

More important, keeping the Sabbath is also an expression of faith. We keep the Sabbath not only for our own recovery and rest, but to show the world our faith in and obedience to God. When we refuse to work and chase worldly things on the Sabbath, we declare to the world that we believe God will supply our needs and that His blessing will fill our lives.

So let us stop once a week, connect with God, seek His will, and enjoy His peace. Let us remember the truth of Isaiah 56:2: only those who keep the Sabbath and keep their hands from doing evil are truly blessed.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you draw near to God on every Sabbath and experience His grace and peace. Amen.
403 Fast Snack: Action Guide. Putting into practice keeping the Lord’s Day worship and enjoying rest in the Lord in daily life requires a clear goal and concrete methods. Here are some suggestions that can help you keep the Lord’s Day worship and enjoy rest in the Lord.
First, we can plan our Lord’s Day schedule ahead of time. This means arranging other activities in advance to make sure we have ample time to take part in the church’s worship and gatherings. We can treat the Lord’s Day as an important time of connecting with God and with brothers and sisters in fellowship, and regard it as a time to meet with God, receive teaching, and encourage one another.
Second, when we get up on the morning of the Lord’s Day, we can begin the day with a heart of thanksgiving and praise. This can be done through Bible reading, prayer, and silence. A good way to connect with God is to read or meditate on a passage of Scripture and think about its truth and application.
Third, after the Lord’s Day worship, we can use time to reflect on and review what we have learned. This can be done by taking notes, sharing with others, or personal reflection. In this way we can understand the message we heard more deeply and apply it in daily life.
In addition, we can look for opportunities to take part in the church’s service and activities. This not only helps us connect with the church, but also gives us a chance to put our faith into practice and help others.
Finally, we can set up a weekly time of rest, focused on meeting with God and relaxing body and mind. This can be a time of seeking spiritual direction, being immersed in activities we love, spending time with family and friends, and so on. Through such worship we can regain strength and peace and refuel for the new week.
These are some concrete and practical methods that can help us put into practice keeping the Lord’s Day worship and enjoying rest in the Lord in daily life. Keeping the Lord’s Day worship and enjoying rest in the Lord is not only a personal practice, but also a journey of connecting with God, growing, and serving. May you experience God’s grace and abundance on this journey and become a Christian full of faith, hope, and love.

t: Blessed Is the One Who Gets Wisdom
v: Happy is the man who finds wisdom, the man who gets understanding.
b: In this verse God tells us how precious wisdom and understanding are. They not only give us blessing, but let us accomplish something in life.

Imagine a farmer who plants a grapevine with patience and wisdom. He knows that growing a fine grapevine takes time and effort. He learns how to prune, fertilize, and irrigate to make sure the vine grows healthy. In the end, when the moment he has been waiting for comes, he harvests delicious grapes and enjoys the fruit of his hard work.

This story tells us that wisdom is like the farmer’s work in the vineyard. If we work hard to learn and use wisdom, we too can harvest the rich fruit of life. Wisdom lets us make the right choices when we face adversity and challenges. It is the compass of our lives.

And understanding is wisdom’s companion. It lets us observe and grasp things keenly. People of understanding know how to adapt to their environment and get along with others, and they can seize opportunities and make wise decisions. Understanding makes our relationships more harmonious and makes us more effective at work and in study.

So, brothers and sisters, let us work hard to pursue wisdom and understanding. This is a process that requires continual learning and growth. We can read the Bible, seek God’s will, and learn through fellowship with wise people. When we have wisdom and understanding, we can better face the challenges of life and be God’s witnesses in the world.

So let us pray together, asking God to give us wisdom and understanding and to use them in our daily lives. May we be those who get wisdom and are blessed, and who show God’s goodness and truth in everyday life.
ah: Pursuing wisdom and understanding in daily life is a process of continual learning and growth. Below I will share some concrete, practical, and effective methods to help you put this pursuit into practice in life.
a: First, it is important to cultivate curiosity. Curiosity drives us to seek knowledge and understand the nature of things. Like an explorer, keeping curiosity about the world will inspire your thinking and widen your horizons. Ask questions every day, look for answers, and keep a thinking attitude.

Second, reading is the key to gaining wisdom. Through books, articles, and online resources, you can learn all kinds of knowledge. Choose high-quality and inspiring reading material, such as philosophy, psychology, or books on wisdom and spiritual life. This will help you open up your thinking and understand life and the world more deeply.

Third, talk with wise people. Conversation with wise people can inspire your thinking, and through their experience and insight, you can learn new viewpoints and methods. Keep good communication with friends, family, or mentors, and share your ideas and learning experiences with each other.

Fourth, store and apply what you learn. The knowledge gained from reading, study, and experience is precious, but knowledge alone without application is limited. Apply what you have learned in daily life, think about how to solve problems, make wise decisions, and practice what you have learned in action.

Finally, reflect and grow regularly. Wisdom and understanding require constant reflection and growth. Regularly examine your own ideas and behavior, and think about how to improve and learn. Give yourself time and space to reflect, and accept challenge and change.

These are concrete ways to practice the pursuit of wisdom and understanding in daily life. By cultivating curiosity, reading, conversation, applying what you learn, and regular reflection, you will be able to keep growing in wisdom and understanding and achieve real results in life. May you be full of faith, hope, and love on this journey of pursuing wisdom!
pr: Ask God to give us wisdom and understanding and to use them in our daily lives. May we be those who get wisdom and are blessed, and who show God’s goodness and truth in everyday life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May God give you wisdom and understanding, so that you can discover His plan and will in life. Amen.

t: Blessed to Hold Fast to Wisdom
v: She is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her. Happy is everyone who retains her.
b: In this passage God reminds us of the importance of holding fast to wisdom, and tells us that all who hold on to wisdom are blessed.

When we speak of wisdom, we might imagine a tree of life. Wisdom is like the root of this tree, giving us wise thinking, right conduct, and divine guidance. This tree of life not only brings fullness of life to us, but lets us be set apart from this world, to be light and salt, bringing blessing and hope to others.

Yet holding fast to wisdom is not easy. This world is full of temptations and testing, and we often face the danger of losing our way and straying onto wrong paths. But God’s purpose in giving us wisdom is to guide us onto the right path and to help us avoid disaster and regret.

It is like a person lost in a forest who does not know which direction to go and can only search aimlessly for a way out. At that time, wisdom is like a bright lamp, lighting the path ahead of him, so that he can regain his direction and find the way home.

In the same way, when we hold fast to wisdom, she becomes the compass of our lives, leading us to find a way out in difficulty, a goal in confusion, and strength in setbacks. Wisdom not only lets us make wise decisions, but also gives us the fruit of patience and wisdom.

So let us hold fast to wisdom every day, and whatever challenge we face, rely on her to guide our steps. When we meet difficulties at work, wisdom will tell us to persevere and never give in. When we meet obstacles in study, wisdom will remind us to keep learning and look for solutions. When we are hurt in relationships, wisdom will teach us forgiveness and tolerance.
ah: Practicing wisdom in daily life is a very important and beneficial goal. I would like to share some methods with you that can help you hold fast to wisdom and apply it in life.
a: First, learn to listen humbly. When we are willing to listen to others’ opinions and advice, we can gain wisdom from their experience. Whether at work or in personal life, respect others’ viewpoints and seek advice from all sides. Through such conduct we can obtain more complete information and make better decisions.

Second, stay calm and rational. Sometimes when we face pressure and difficulty, we may become emotional or act on impulse. But staying calm and rational is the key to wisdom. When we can think about problems calmly and take calm action, we can make wiser choices.

Also, cultivate curiosity and an attitude of learning. Wisdom is not only about knowledge, but about continuous learning and growth. Keeping curiosity can spark our interest in new things and inspire our thinking. Have an attitude of learning, keep pursuing new knowledge and skills, and apply them in real life.

Finally, learn from mistakes. Everyone makes mistakes, but wise people can learn and grow from them. When we make a mistake, do not be dejected or complain. Instead, reflect on our own conduct, understand the cause of the mistake, and work to improve ourselves.

In summary, holding fast to wisdom requires humble listening, calm and rationality, curiosity and an attitude of learning, and learning from mistakes. Through these methods, we can better follow and practice wisdom in daily life and achieve concrete and effective results. May you find wisdom’s guidance on this journey!
pr:
Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us today’s message about holding fast to wisdom. May Your words be a guide in our lives and help us practice wisdom in daily life.
Lord, we ask You to give us a humble, listening heart, so that we can respect others’ viewpoints and gain wisdom from their experience. May we not only listen to others’ advice but also humbly accept guidance, so that we can make wise decisions when we face choices.
We ask You to give us a calm and rational heart, so that we can remain composed in adversity and under pressure. When we face difficulty and conflict, may Your wisdom guide us to take the right action rather than be swayed by emotion.
Lord, we ask You to give us curiosity and an attitude of learning, so that we can keep pursuing knowledge and growth. May Your wisdom inspire us to think and explore new things and to apply what we learn in real life.
Finally, we ask You to help us learn from our mistakes. We all make mistakes, but give us a humble and wise heart, so that we can draw lessons from our errors, grow, and improve ourselves.
Thank You, Heavenly Father, for giving us guidance to hold fast to wisdom. Help us practice these principles of wisdom in daily life and be Your witnesses of light. We pray in the name of Jesus, amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you hold fast to wisdom today and be a keeper of the tree of life. May you show God’s wisdom and love in every circumstance and be a witness to His grace. Amen.

t: Blessed to Listen to Wisdom
v: Blessed is the man who hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at my door posts.
b: In this verse God calls us to listen to the voice of wisdom, to watch at the gate, and to wait beside the doorposts. This is an extremely important instruction, because only when we are willing to draw near to wisdom and listen to her teaching can we truly receive blessing.

Suppose we are in a house filled with thick smoke that makes it hard to breathe. In such a situation we urgently need a suitable escape route to get away from this dangerous environment. Wisdom is like a smoke escape guide in our daily lives. She can lead us out of the maze of being lost and confused and bring us into the land of God’s grace and promise.

A young man named Xiangming often felt confused when facing choices. He saw friends around him pursuing material pleasures while he longed for a more meaningful life. One day he met a wise teacher, and under her guidance he learned how to treat others with love and how to act humbly and generously. These wise teachings made Xiangming’s life more valuable and purposeful.

As Proverbs 8:34 says, the one who listens to wisdom, watches for her, and waits for her will surely be blessed. When we listen attentively to the voice of wisdom each day and let God’s word guide our lives, we will receive the abundance and blessing God has promised. We can walk a road full of faith, hope, and love, and become a blessing to those around us.

Let us think together: in our daily lives, are we truly willing to listen to wisdom’s teaching? Are we willing to look attentively to her guidance? Are we willing to stop and wait for her revelation before every decision?

By listening to the voice of wisdom we can find answers in confusion and shelter in the storm. May we ask God every day to give us a keen spirit and a heart that listens to wisdom, so that we can be His disciples and live out faith, hope, and love in daily life.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you be blessed on the road of listening to wisdom, and may you listen to wisdom’s voice when you face choices and act with faith, hope, and love. Amen.

t: Blessed to Have Transgressions Forgiven
v: Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
b: In everyone’s life it is unavoidable to make mistakes and to sin. We may feel regret, self-reproach, or even despair because of our faults. Yet God’s word reminds us that when we sincerely repent and ask Him for forgiveness, we are blessed.

Think of Peter, Jesus’ disciple. After the Last Supper, when Jesus was arrested and about to be crucified, Peter denied Jesus three times. Peter felt deep remorse and shame, and he thought he would never again have a chance to receive God’s forgiveness.

Yet after Jesus rose from the dead, Jesus came to find Peter Himself. Jesus asked him, “Peter, do you love Me?” Peter answered, “Lord, You know that I love You.” Jesus asked the same question three times, and each time Peter answered firmly. This was the opportunity Jesus gave Peter, so that he could express his love for Him again and receive forgiveness.

This story tells us that when we make mistakes and turn away from God, God not only forgives us but also looks for us and gives us the chance to rebuild our relationship with Him. God’s lovingkindness and grace are endless. When we sincerely repent to Him, He will cover our sins and grant forgiveness, so that we can once again have spiritual peace and joy.

In our daily lives we also meet all kinds of difficulties and failures. Sometimes we may feel despair because of our own mistakes or be troubled by sin. Yet this passage reminds us that God’s forgiveness is real.

When we are honest with God about our faults and seek His forgiveness and help, we can regain spiritual freedom and joy. God’s forgiveness not only gives our souls comfort, but also gives us more strength in daily life.

So whatever mistakes we have made and however far we have turned from God’s way, let us not stay sunk in the trap of sin, but bravely ask God for forgiveness. His loving hand is always stretched out to us, waiting for us to turn back. When we receive God’s forgiveness, we will regain freedom and be renewed in strength, and once again return to God’s path and follow His will.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you. May you find forgiveness and the covering of your sins in every mistake and setback. May you experience God’s grace and love and be that blessed person whose transgressions are forgiven. Amen.

t: Blessed Not to Be Counted Guilty
v: Blessed is the man to whom the LORD doesn’t impute iniquity, in whose spirit there is no deceit.
b: In this passage God tells an important truth: the person in whom there is no deceit, and whom God regards as without guilt, is blessed.

We live in a world full of deceit and trickery, where people often neglect the truth and lose themselves, seeking fleeting pleasure and selfish gain. We too may have made mistakes and been entangled in sin, feeling weary and in despair. But in God’s eyes, as long as we are sincere in heart, have no deceit, and are willing to confess and repent, He will not count us guilty. What great blessing this is!

Let us think: how many times have we chosen deceit and dishonest ways to deal with difficulty and testing? Or deceived others for our own benefit? Such conduct only leaves us feeling empty and discouraged inside, and God cannot be with us.

But if we choose to face our mistakes honestly and truthfully, and seek God’s forgiveness and redemption, God will bless us. When we repent and correct our mistakes, God’s grace and mercy will fill our lives and bring peace and joy. We will experience God’s guiltless love and mercy, and no longer be afraid in difficulty.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: May you face your own conduct and challenges with a sincere heart every day, and find peace and joy in God’s grace. May you be a person without deceit, counted guiltless in God’s eyes, for such a person is truly blessed. Amen.

t: Blessed to Be Counted Righteous
v: Even as David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works:
b: “Dear family, peace! Welcome to share this soul snack together. Today God’s word says to us: ‘Even as David also pronounces blessing on the man to whom God counts righteousness apart from works.’ (Romans 4:6)”

Today we are going to talk about the blessing of being counted righteous. In this world we often judge ourselves by our own conduct, or are swayed by others’ opinions. We strive for perfection, yet always feel that we have failed and are not good enough.

But God tells us that being counted righteous is a wonderful thing. It is not based on our conduct, but on God’s lovingkindness and grace toward us. Like David, who in the Bible was a man counted righteous by God, though he committed great sin, he believed in God’s forgiveness and mercy.

In life we often meet setbacks and failures, and may even feel that we are worthless. But when we accept God’s grace and mercy and believe that He counts us righteous, we will feel boundless joy and freedom.

Like a prisoner set free from jail, we can regain our freedom. We are no longer bound by past mistakes and sins, but can live a spiritual life. This is exciting news, because no matter what we have done, God is willing to accept us and give complete forgiveness and a new beginning.

Let us live out the identity of being counted righteous in daily life. Whether at work, at home, or in social settings, we can show God’s love and grace. When we treat others with love, care for their needs, and are willing to forgive their faults, we become witnesses of being counted righteous.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you all. May you deeply experience God’s grace and mercy every day and bring this love and hope to others. May you be counted righteous and enjoy true blessing. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One Whose Sin Is Not Counted
v: Blessed is the man whom the Lord will by no means charge with sin.”
b: In this verse we see God’s lovingkindness and grace. He does not count our sins against us. Instead, in His great love He receives us and gives us true blessing.

Every one of us makes mistakes and falls into sin at times, yet God is willing to forgive us. What He gives us is a chance and grace to get back on the right path. Like loving parents, when their child does wrong, they do not blame or reject the child forever. They give the child a chance to make it right and guide him with love.
In the same way, God wants us to learn and grow from our mistakes. He does not hold our faults against us on purpose. He is willing to see us repent and walk again on the right road.

In life we often face all kinds of difficulties and challenges. Sometimes our mistakes and sins leave us feeling hopeless and discouraged. But when we understand the truth of this verse, we see that God is a loving God who is willing to give us new hope and strength.

Let us remember that whatever mistakes we have made, God is willing to receive us and give us new life and hope. Just as the sun rises every day and drives away the darkness, God’s lovingkindness and grace can untangle us from our sins and set us free.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: when you feel lost and hopeless, may you remember that God is a loving Father who is willing to receive you and give you new hope. When you are accused of sin, may you hold fast to God’s grace and lovingkindness and receive strength and encouragement from them. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One God Corrects
v: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.
b: In this passage we see that God’s correction is actually a blessing. When God disciplines us, we should not resent it or complain, because this is the way He cares for us and shapes us.

A farmer planted grapevines in his field. One day he noticed that the leaves of the vines were shading too much of the sun, so the grapes could not ripen fully. To save the grapes, he cut away some of the branches and let more sunlight in.

This story tells us that the farmer pruned for the good of the grapes, so that they could ripen fully. In the same way, when God corrects us, He does not act out of malice but for our growth and good.

Sometimes, when we have taken a wrong road, God uses difficulties and challenges to change our direction. He may cut away wrong habits, harmful relationships, or useless ways from our lives, so that more light can enter.

So when God corrects us, we should keep faith and hope, believing that He is shaping us to be more like Him. Let us receive His discipline with thankful hearts, for it is an expression of His love and care for us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: when God corrects you, may you keep faith and hope, understanding that it shows His love and care for you. May God’s word be fulfilled in your life and bring you abundant life and lasting joy. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One God Disciplines
v: Blessed is the man whom you discipline, LORD, and teach out of your law,
b: In this passage, God reminds us that being disciplined by Him is a blessing. When we meet challenges, difficulties, or failure, we should not be discouraged or despair. Instead, let us hold on to faith, because these experiences are what God uses to teach and shape us.

Like a loving father who keeps teaching his children, God disciplines us with the same love. His teaching comes from His law, which tells us how to live. When we keep His law, we will see God’s blessing and grace flowing in our lives.

When we face hardship, such as losing a job, illness, or trouble in relationships, these are opportunities God gives us to grow and learn. Just as a rough diamond must go through pressure and cutting to become a dazzling gem, our hardships are opportunities to shape our character.

In this process, God’s grace becomes our shelter and strength. When we trust in Him, He gives us courage and hope so that we can face adversity and challenge. We are no longer merely trapped in difficulty, but stand in God’s grace and watch His plan unfold in our lives.

So let us treasure God’s discipline and welcome every challenge with a thankful heart. Let us remember that being disciplined by God is a blessing, because it is an expression of His love and care for us. Trust His plan, hold fast to faith, and hope for His promises to be fulfilled in our lives.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you experience God’s grace and strength as He disciplines you. May your faith and hope grow because of it, bringing you more blessing and peace. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One Whose Quiver Is Full
v: Happy is the man who has his quiver full of them. They won’t be disappointed when they speak with their enemies in the gate.
b: In applying this verse, the one whose quiver is full can be seen as a picture of someone full of ability and talent. Imagine we are going to shoot arrows, but there are only a few arrows in the quiver. Our ability would be very limited. But when the quiver is full of arrows, we have more chances to hit the target. This is why the one with a full quiver is called blessed: when he faces challenges he is not put to shame, but meets them with confidence.

In life we also meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties, perhaps pressure at work or problems in relationships. But when we are full of talent and ability, we can face these difficulties firmly. Like a quiver full of arrows, we can solve problems accurately and not be ashamed.

Let us think about how to fill our quiver with arrows. First, we can keep learning and growing. By reading books, taking courses, or talking with experienced people, we can continually improve our skills and knowledge. Second, we can discover our potential, understand our strengths and gifts, and develop them to the fullest. Finally, we can rely on God’s help, because He gives us spiritual gifts and wisdom to serve more effectively in every area of life.

Dear family, let us remember that a full quiver is a blessing, because it means we have enough ability and talent to meet the challenges of life. However great the difficulties we face, we can stand at the city gate with confidence and speak with our enemies without being ashamed.
Today, let us pursue a life with a full quiver! Let us keep learning and growing, discover our potential, and rely on God’s help.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you become one whose quiver is full, full of faith, hope, and love. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One Who Has Mercy on the Poor
v: He who despises his neighbor sins, but he who has pity on the poor is blessed.
b: God’s word reminds us that our attitude toward others is extremely important. When we look down on or ignore the neighbors around us, we sin. But when we show mercy and care to those in poverty, we are blessed.

There was once a rich merchant who had a very kind neighbor, and he always cared about this neighbor’s poverty. Whenever he saw his neighbor in trouble, he reached out to help. This merchant knew that even a small bit of help could bring his neighbor great comfort and joy.

One day the merchant heard about someone in need, a poor single mother. She and her children were in desperate straits. The merchant did not hesitate. He contacted the family at once and provided food, clothing, and other necessities.

The single mother was deeply grateful, and she was touched by such generosity and love. She saw the merchant’s mercy and began to be filled with confidence and hope for life. The merchant’s mercy and care changed the destiny of this family and brought them a new life.

This story tells us that the one who has mercy on the poor is blessed. When we look at others with love and compassion, we can not only change their lives but also feel God’s blessing. God calls us to treat people with mercy and care, and to reach out when they are in need.
Let us think each day: in our daily life, do we have opportunities to reach out to the poor and those who need help? When we act with mercy and love, we will experience God’s blessing and abundance.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you receive rich blessing and joy as you show mercy to the poor. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One Who Cares for the Poor
v: Blessed is he who considers the poor. The LORD will deliver him in the day of evil.
b: In our lives we often meet difficulties and challenges, and sometimes we even feel poor and helpless. But this verse tells us that when we care for the poor, we are blessed. This is not only about material help, but also an expression of care and love. There was a young man named Dexiu who came from a poor family. From childhood he had learned to share and to help others. Even when he had only a little, he was willing to share it. This attitude won the respect and admiration of the people around him.

One day an old man was in trouble and had no money to buy medicine for his illness. When Dexiu heard of it, he did not hesitate. He took out his savings and gave them to the old man. A few days later, Dexiu received an unexpected sum of money, enough for him to go to university. Dexiu thanked God for His blessing and understood that caring for the poor is a blessed thing to do. In the same way, in our lives, when we can help those in difficulty, we too will receive God’s deliverance and blessing.

This may be through giving to a charity, or by spending time talking with and keeping company with those in need. Whether what we do is great or small, as long as it comes from love and care, God will see what we give and bless us. Dear family, let us care for the poor with love and concern, and bring them hope and help. In this process we too will feel God’s blessing and deliverance.
a: Give

When we are able, we can give money, food, or other resources to poor people in need. This can be done by taking part in charity events, supporting charitable organizations, or contacting poor families in the community directly.
Volunteer

Use your time and skills to take part in volunteer service and give practical help to poor people. This could be working at a food bank, holding educational activities, offering job training, and so on.
Offer support and care
Besides material aid, poor people also need emotional support and care. We can spend time talking with them, listen to their stories, and offer encouragement and comfort.
Promote education

Education is the key to changing a person’s destiny. We can provide funding or resources to help poor people receive education or skills training, so as to improve their job opportunities and standard of living.
Reflect on our spending

We can reflect on our own spending habits, reduce waste, and use our resources where they matter more. This not only saves resources, but the money saved can be used to help the poor. Through these practical ways, we can live out the blessing of caring for the poor in daily life and become God’s hands and feet, reaching out to those in need. Whether in small things or great, every practical action can bring hope and change.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us abundant blessings in our lives. Help us realize that these blessings are not only for our own enjoyment, but so that we may become Your messengers, caring for and helping the poor.
We ask You to give us wisdom and strength to live out the blessing of caring for the poor through practical action. Help us give what we can of money, food, and resources, so that this help truly reaches those in need. May we also take part in volunteer service, using our time and skills to help them, giving them practical support and care.
We ask You to guide us in the work of promoting education, helping poor people receive education and skills training to change their destiny. Let us reflect on our spending, reduce waste, use our resources where they matter more, and use the money we save in the work of caring for the poor.
Thank You, Heavenly Father, for giving us the opportunity to be Your hands and feet and to bring hope and change. Give us firm faith, hope, and love, so that we may practice the blessing of caring for the poor in our daily lives.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: as you care for the poor, may you experience God’s power and mercy. Amen!

t: Blessed Are the Children of the Righteous
v: A righteous man walks in integrity. Blessed are his children after him.
b: This passage tells us that when we keep God’s moral standards and live with integrity, both we and our children will be blessed. But what does this really mean? In a small village there was a farmer named David. He was a devout Christian who lived each day according to God’s will. He was honest and trustworthy, glad to help others, and full of love and care for people.

David’s farm was famous in the village for its abundance. His crops grew strong and the harvest was rich. His family was also very happy. His wife worked hard beside him, and his children were dutiful and respected by people.

When David’s children grew up, they too inherited their father’s faith and values. They became a family that prospered not only materially, but whose members were also in harmony with one another. They treated others with love and care and continued to live uprightly.

This story tells us that when we keep God’s moral standards and live with integrity, we receive not only material blessing, but our family and children are also blessed because of our faith and values.

In real life we may face all kinds of difficulties and challenges. But when we persist in walking the right road and trust in God’s plan and grace, we can rest assured that God will surely bless our effort and faithfulness.

So let us face every person and every situation each day with kindness, integrity, and love. Whether at work, at home, or in social settings, let us lead by example and be righteous people who walk in integrity.
ah: From Proverbs 20:7 we can learn an important lesson: a righteous man walks in his integrity, and blessed are his children after him! This tells us that our conduct and character have a deep influence on ourselves and on our children. In daily life, we can put this truth into practice in the following ways:
a: Build good values

To become a righteous person who walks in integrity, we first need to settle our values. These values should include honesty, integrity, love, and justice. When we have clear values, we can better guide our conduct.
Develop good habits

To become righteous, we need to develop good habits. This includes rising early every day, reading Scripture and praying, and seeking wisdom and guidance. We also need to cultivate habits of kindness, tolerance, and concern for others. Through these habits we can keep improving our character.
Pass on virtue to the next generation

According to the teaching of Proverbs, the children of the righteous are blessed. We should pass on virtue and right values to our children. This can be done by giving them a good education, building a deep relationship with them, and being an example to them. In this way, our children will benefit from our integrity and carry it on in their own lives.
Show the love of Jesus

As righteous people who walk in integrity, we should strive to show the love of Jesus. This means not only showing love in our own lives, but sharing that love with others. We can express it by helping those in need, caring for the vulnerable, and taking part in volunteer service. In this way we can not only improve our own lives and the lives of others, but also plant good seeds in the next generation. In conclusion, Proverbs 20:7 reminds us that the righteous man who walks in integrity and his children are blessed. We can put this lesson into practice by building good values, developing good habits, passing on virtue to the next generation, and showing the love of Jesus. Let us strive to be righteous people who walk in integrity, bringing blessing to ourselves and our children!
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for the teaching of Proverbs 20:7, which helps us understand that the righteous man who walks in integrity and his children are blessed. Help us put this truth into practice in our daily lives.
We ask You to help us build good values, so that we may have the lovely character of honesty, integrity, love, and justice. Give us wisdom and guidance, so that we can rise early every day, read Scripture and pray, and seek Your face.
Help us develop good habits, so that we become kind, tolerant, and caring people. Help us pass on virtue to the next generation, giving them a good education, building a deep relationship with them, and being an example to them.
We ask You to let us show the love of Jesus, not only in our own lives but sharing that love with others. Help us care for the vulnerable, help those in need, and take part in volunteer service, to show the love of Jesus.
Thank You for Your promise that the righteous man who walks in integrity and his children are blessed. Show Your grace and blessing in our lives and let this blessing be passed on to our children.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you be blessed as you keep God’s moral standards and live with integrity. Amen.

t: All Nations Will Call You Blessed
v: “All nations shall call you blessed, for you will be a delightful land,” says the LORD of Armies.
b: This passage reminds us that when we walk with God and live out His purpose, our lives and the world around us will be filled with joy and blessing. God’s heart is for us to be a source of joy, so that all the nations will call us blessed.

When we welcome strangers with love and care, they will see God’s grace and love in us. It is like a traveler lost in a desolate desert who suddenly meets a kind benefactor. The benefactor points him in the right direction and gives him some water and food, and the traveler is moved to tears and thanks God for sending him this angel-like helper. That benefactor is us, the ones who bring people guidance and help.

In the same way, when we show faith, hope, and love at work, at school, and at home, we become light and salt in our surroundings. Think of a child who meets difficulty at school and sees a classmate facing challenges with confidence and optimism. The child is inspired and begins to believe he too can overcome his difficulties, because he has seen a living example.
So let us be such people, the good news that those around us need. Wherever we are and whatever we do, we have the chance to be messengers of joy, letting God’s grace and love fill our lives.
ah: In our daily lives, we all hope to be called blessed. According to the words of Malachi 3:12, the Lord of Armies tells us that when we live joyfully in the land God has given, the nations will praise us as blessed. So how can we put this principle into practice in our daily lives? Let us do it in the following ways:
a: An attitude of gratitude

Keeping a thankful heart is the key to living the way of joy. Each morning when you get up, take a moment to think about thanking God for everything He has given you, great or small. This will lift your mood and begin your day with gladness.
Love for others

Make loving others the purpose of your life. Use your time, ability, and resources to help others, especially those near you who need help. By loving others, you will experience more joy and satisfaction.
Enjoying nature

Connect with nature and sense God’s creativity and beauty in it. Spend time walking outdoors, watching the sunrise or sunset, or enjoying the gifts of nature with family and friends. Such contact will bring your soul comfort and joy.
Learning to forgive

Forgiveness is an act that frees the heart. When we learn to forgive others’ wrongs, we can also let go of our own pain and the burden within us. This brings joy to others and to ourselves, and draws us closer to the image of God.
Continuing to grow

Our relationship with God is a process of continual growth. By reading the Bible, praying, and taking part in church activities, you can cultivate spiritual depth with God. As you develop spiritually, you will see more clearly the joy and blessing God brings into your life. Whatever our circumstances, we can become people who are called blessed by these means. When we live out our faith with joy and gratitude, we become God’s witnesses and lead others to experience God’s love and joy together. May we grow in God’s grace every day and be called blessed among all the nations. Let us pray together, dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us blessing and grace every day. I thank You for making us blessed people, and under Your guidance we can put this principle into practice in our daily lives. Lord, help us keep an attitude of gratitude, so that each morning when we rise we think of thanking You for all You have given us. May our hearts be made more cheerful and full of joy because of it. Guide us to love others and to share care and generosity with those around us who need help. May our actions bring joy and satisfaction and become Your witness. Lord, let us connect with nature and sense Your creativity and beauty in it. May we spend time walking outdoors, watching the sunrise or sunset, and sharing these gifts with family and friends, so that our souls are comforted and gladdened. Help us learn to forgive and release the burden of the heart. Let us forgive others’ wrongs and let go of our own pain and the burden within us. This draws us closer to Your image and also brings joy and peace. Lord, help us keep growing in Your grace. Through reading the Bible, praying, and taking part in church activities, lead us to cultivate a deeper relationship with You. May we see clearly the joy and blessing You bring into our lives and become Your witnesses. Lord, may we grow in Your grace every day and be called blessed among all the nations. Thank You for continually leading us and for making us channels of Your love and joy. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you be a blessing from God, a person others call blessed. May you spread joy and love every day and be an encouragement and hope to others. Amen.

t: Blessed Are the Poor in Spirit
v: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
b: “Dear family, peace to you! Welcome to share in Soul Snacks. Today God’s word speaks to us: ‘Matt. 5:3 Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.’

In this passage we receive a very important revelation: the humble in spirit are blessed. To be humble in spirit means to be willing to accept teaching, glad to listen to others’ advice, and ready to admit our own shortcomings. Such people are given the grace of the Kingdom of Heaven, and they can experience spiritual abundance and eternal joy.

There was a young student. He had always done very well in his studies, and was also outstanding in sports and in relationships. His confidence rose accordingly, and he even became somewhat self-satisfied. But one day he met a classmate who was better than he was. This classmate not only surpassed him in grades, but also excelled in sports and the arts.

The young man felt discouraged and defeated, because his pride had been struck. But he did not give up or become jealous. Instead, he humbly learned from this classmate and humbly accepted his guidance and advice. He began to work at overcoming his weaknesses and no longer relied on his past achievements. In the end, he made greater breakthroughs in his studies and relationships and grew at a deeper level.

This story tells us that humility of spirit is a very important virtue. When we know how to be humble, we can accept guidance and criticism from others and live in peace with them. In the same way, in our relationship with God, humility is also necessary. We need to lay down pride and self-righteousness, admit our imperfection, and be willing to listen to and obey God’s teaching.

So let us remind ourselves every day to stay humble, learning and growing continually. When we humbly seek God’s purpose, we will find the blessing of the Kingdom of Heaven welling up from the depths of our spirit, and our lives will be full of faith, hope, and love.
a: Accept your imperfection
The humble in spirit first accept their limits and imperfections. They understand that they do not know everything or have every ability, and they are willing to learn from others.
Listen openly to others

The humble in spirit know how to respect others’ views and opinions. They listen to what others say, do not easily interrupt or judge, but keep an open mind and draw inspiration from others’ experience and wisdom.
Humbly admit your mistakes
The humble in spirit have a modest attitude and are willing to admit their mistakes. They do not deny or cover up their faults to save face, but bravely face them and learn from them.
Learn and grow

The humble in spirit keep learning and growing. They learn not only from others but also take in knowledge and wisdom from books, the internet, courses, and other resources, continually improving their abilities and skills.
Seek guidance and advice

The humble in spirit know how to ask others for guidance and advice. They realize they may not be able to solve every problem alone, so they humbly ask experts, elders, or experienced people for help and gain insight from their counsel.
Generously share knowledge and resources

The humble in spirit gladly share the knowledge and resources they have learned with others. They understand that sharing not only helps others grow but also improves their own understanding and memory.
Respect others’ expertise

The humble in spirit respect the expertise and specialties of others. They are willing to admit that they may not be experts in some field, and they gladly learn from professionals to increase their knowledge and skills.
See challenges as opportunities

The humble in spirit see challenges as opportunities for growth and learning. They are not discouraged by difficulties but face them with a positive attitude, believing that overcoming challenges will make them stronger and wiser. Blessed are the poor in spirit, because they can live with an attitude of humility, respect for others, and continual learning and growth. By practicing these ways, we can build healthier, richer, and more meaningful relationships, and also be more fulfilled in self-improvement and achievement.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us a humble heart, so that we can humbly face our own imperfection. May we accept our limits in daily life and be willing to learn from others.
We ask You to give us the ability to listen openly to others, so that we can respect their views and opinions. May we not easily interrupt or judge others, but keep an open mind and draw inspiration from their experience and wisdom.
Help us humbly admit our mistakes, and not deny or cover up our faults to save face. May we bravely face them and learn from them, so that we grow and improve.
Give us a heart that keeps learning and growing. May we learn not only from others but also take in knowledge and wisdom from books, the internet, courses, and other resources, continually improving our abilities and skills.
Guide us to seek guidance and advice, and humbly ask experts, elders, or experienced people for help. May we gain insight from their counsel and benefit greatly in our lives.
Give us a generous heart to share knowledge and resources, so that we gladly share what we have learned with others. May we understand that sharing not only helps others grow but also improves our own understanding and memory.
Help us respect the expertise and specialties of others. May we admit that we may not be experts in some field, and gladly learn from professionals to increase our knowledge and skills.
Help us see challenges as opportunities, face difficulties with a positive attitude, and believe that overcoming challenges will make us stronger and wiser.
May we live with an attitude of humility, respect for others, and continual learning and growth, and build healthier, richer, and more meaningful relationships. Help us be more fulfilled in self-improvement and achievement.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you stay humble and poor in spirit every day, and experience spiritual abundance in your relationships with God and with others. Amen.”

t: Blessed Are Those Who Mourn
v: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
b: This verse tells us that those who mourn are blessed, because they will receive God’s comfort. In life we inevitably face setbacks, losses, and pain. It may be the loss of a loved one, the loss of a job, or a health problem. These difficulties leave us grieved and heartbroken, as if there were no end.

But here Jesus tells us we need not despair, because God will comfort us. Just as a mother holds her child when he falls, God surrounds us with His love and compassion in our hardest moments. He knows our pain, and He is willing to be with us.

A seed was buried in the soil, and alone it grew into a little tree. But suddenly a great wind blew it over, and it felt helpless and sad. Then spring came, rain soaked the earth, and the sapling stood up again. It gradually grew into a tall, strong tree, with thick branches and leaves that brought people coolness and shelter.

This parable reminds us not to lose hope when we suffer grief and pain in life. Like that little tree, we too will rise again and grow strong. God will give us strength and comfort, help us find our smile again, and give us courage to face the future.
So let us believe this truth, that those who mourn are blessed. When we face difficulty and pain, let us not lose faith. God is always beside us, and His love and comfort are always with us.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you find comfort in mourning, find hope in difficulty, and have faith to face the future. Amen.

t: Blessed Are the Gentle
v: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
b: In this busy and competitive world, gentleness is often overlooked or seen as weakness. Yet this passage reminds us that true blessing comes from having a gentle heart.

Imagine a gardener working in a garden full of thorns and weeds. With gentle hands he diligently pulls the weeds, prunes the trees, and carefully tends every flower. His heart is full of love, and he treats everything in nature with respect and care. In the end he sees the garden bloom in beauty, all the thorns replaced, and every flower full of life.

Our lives are the same. When we treat others with a gentle heart, we can heal wounds, resolve quarrels, and plant seeds of kindness and love. Gentleness gives off a silent power that can open hearts, link discouraged people to hope, and fill life with positive energy.

The gentle do not only receive blessing in this life. On their spiritual journey they also inherit the land God has promised. We are called to treat one another with gentleness, because gentleness is a display of the image of God and a key to our relationship with Him.
When we treat others with gentleness and kindness, we show God’s love and grace. Such conduct not only brings comfort and hope to others, but also fills our own hearts with peace and joy.
So let us strive every day to be gentle people, treating others with a heart full of love. When we do, we will experience the blessing God has promised and become His light in this world.
ah: We can put into practice “Blessed are the gentle” in daily life in the following ways:
a: Respect others
Treat others with respect and tolerance, whatever their views, background, or habits. Respect is the foundation for building good relationships and promoting harmony.
Control your emotions
The gentle do not easily lose their temper or revile others. When facing challenges or conflict, stay calm and rational and solve problems with a peaceful mind.
Respond kindly
Respond to others’ words and actions with goodwill. Do not hurt others with harsh words, but treat them with understanding and care.
Be patient and forgiving
Having a gentle heart means being able to bear with others’ shortcomings and faults. Learn to forgive others’ mistakes and give them a chance to make things right.
Build a harmonious environment
In the family, the workplace, and the community, work to create a harmonious environment. Through communication, cooperation, and sharing, promote the growth of relationships.
Serve others

Be glad to help others and care about their needs. Whether offering practical help or emotional support, you can show the quality of gentleness. These ways not only put the quality of gentleness into practice, but also build harmonious relationships and promote spiritual growth and one another’s well-being. May you use these ways in your daily life to practice gentleness and experience the blessing a Christian should have.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for guiding us in how to become gentle people.
May we treat others with respect and tolerance,
and control our emotions and avoid losing our temper easily.
Help us respond to others’ words and actions with goodwill,
and learn to bear with and forgive their mistakes.
May we build harmonious environments in our families, workplaces, and communities,
and gladly serve others and care about their needs.
Bless us, so that we may become gentle people
and experience the blessing that gentleness brings.
We ask in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you be a gentle person, and in daily life and on your spiritual journey may you give off God’s love and the power of faith, hope, and love. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Who Hunger and Thirst for Righteousness
v: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be filled.
b: In this verse the Lord Jesus tells us that those who long to pursue the way of God are blessed. They will not only be satisfied, but will receive abundant promise and blessing.

In this world we are often troubled by all kinds of confusion and temptation, and we long to find the true meaning and purpose of life. Some may look for satisfaction in money, power, or fame, but in the end find that none of these can bring true satisfaction.

Yet when we long for God, and long to understand His word and His ways, God promises that we will surely be satisfied. We will receive spiritual fullness, and the pleasure and joy of an intimate relationship with God.

It is like a person traveling in the wilderness, longing to find a source of water to quench his thirst. Though he passes through many hardships and winding roads, because he keeps on seeking, he finally finds a clear spring. In the same way, when we hunger and thirst after God’s righteousness and truth, God will surely satisfy our souls and fill us with joy and peace.

So let us long for God’s ways every day, and long for God’s grace and truth. As we strive to seek, learn, and live out God’s word, we will be continually filled by the abundant God, and we will be able to share this love and joy with the people around us.
ah: Dear family, let us follow the action guide below. In daily life we can follow the guidance of Matthew 5:6 and bring a heart that hungers and thirsts for righteousness into our conduct and attitudes. Here are some specific ways that can help brothers and sisters put this principle into practice in daily life:
a: Cultivate a longing for truth

We can enrich our knowledge of the faith by reading the Bible regularly, joining Bible study groups, or taking part in church gatherings. By studying God’s word, we can understand God’s will more deeply and adjust our way of life according to the teaching of Scripture.
Pursue justice and integrity

Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness pursue justice, fairness, and integrity. They strive to keep God’s commandments and gladly do good. In daily life we can reflect on whether our words and actions are in line with God’s will, and look for opportunities to help others and serve the community.
Deny yourself to serve others

Those who hunger and thirst for righteousness are willing to give up their own comfort and interests to care for and help those in need. We can actively look for opportunities to serve others, for example by volunteering, donating goods or time, or giving financial support.
Ask God to lead
In everything we should seek God’s leading through prayer and devotion. As our relationship with God grows closer, we can hear His voice more keenly and understand what He wants us to do.
Encourage one another to pursue God’s righteousness

As a Christian community, we should encourage and support one another and pursue God’s righteousness together. By sharing our own journeys of faith and testimonies, we can inspire one another and grow together. These ways are only a beginning. When we actively pursue a life that hungers and thirsts for righteousness, God will surely, according to His promise, give us spiritual fullness. Let us live out a Christian witness every day with a heart that longs for truth, pursues righteousness, and is determined to give itself up to serve others.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for pointing out to us the way of hungering and thirsting for righteousness. We ask You to give us a heart that longs for truth, a will to pursue justice and integrity, and a willingness to deny ourselves and serve others. Help us seek Your leading in daily life, and encourage and support one another as we pursue Your righteousness together. According to Your promise, may we receive spiritual fullness. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you find rich satisfaction on the road of pursuing God. Through God’s grace, may you become a witness full of joy and hope, able to share God’s love with others in your life. Amen.

t: Blessed Are the Merciful
v: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
b: The word mercy appears many times in the Bible, and it stands for care, compassion, and love. God wants us to treat others with a heart of mercy, because when we show mercy to others, God will show mercy to us. This is a truth full of faith, hope, and love.

One cold winter day, an elderly woman was walking down the street. As she went along, she suddenly saw a homeless man huddled shivering in a corner by the road. The woman stopped and looked at this poor man, and she felt a deep compassion.

The woman went up to him, gave him some money from her pocket, and gave him a warm smile. The man felt her mercy and love, and a light of hope appeared on his face. The woman’s act of mercy gave the man faith and hope, and made him believe that life still held good possibilities.

In our own lives we too can show a heart of mercy like this woman. When we see others in need, we should not stop at sympathy but really act to help them. It might be a word of comfort, a helping hand, or sharing our resources and time. When we treat others with a merciful heart, we not only help them, but even more importantly we ourselves receive mercy.
Let us think: in our daily lives, is there someone who needs our mercy and care? Whether friends, family, or strangers near us, everyone can be someone to whom we show mercy.
a: Be kind to others
Learn to treat others with kindness and friendliness. Whether family, friends, or strangers, we should give them respect and care.
Let go of prejudice
Whatever their race, social status, or background, we should have an inclusive attitude. Whatever others’ faults or shortcomings, let us look at them with a heart of mercy.
Sense others’ needs
Pay attention to others’ needs in good time and strive to help. This might be a smile, a word of encouragement, or a practical action to solve someone’s difficulty.
Forgive others
When others fail us or offend us, we should learn to forgive. Forgiveness is a way of setting ourselves free, and it is also mercy toward others.
Share God’s love

Through actions and words we can show God’s mercy to us and share this love with others. This can be reaching out a hand in hard times, or giving encouragement and blessing when it is needed. By putting these ways into practice, we will be able to live out the value of mercy in daily life and experience God’s mercy. In the process we will also find that we receive more blessing, because showing mercy to others is conduct that God delights in and rewards. May we face the world every day with mercy and love and become witnesses to the gospel.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us this opportunity today to come before You and express our love and gratitude to You. Lord, we ask You to give us a merciful heart, so that we treat others with kindness and friendliness. Help us let go of prejudice and see others with an inclusive heart, whatever their race, social status, or background. Help us sense others’ needs and gladly offer help.
Lord, give us strength and wisdom to forgive others. When we face others’ faults or offenses, teach us to look at them with a heart of mercy and to learn to truly forgive. Help us share Your love, showing Your mercy to us through our actions and words, and sharing this love with others.
Lord, we ask You to keep us living out the value of mercy in our daily lives. Make us witnesses to the gospel, so that our conduct and words both show Your glory. Thank You for giving us this mission. May we face the world every day with mercy and love.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: as you look for opportunities to help others, may you be full of faith, hope, and love. May you become a messenger of mercy, bringing hope and comfort to others. Amen.

t: Blessed Are the Pure in Heart
v: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
b: In this passage Jesus tells us that the pure in heart are blessed. So what is a pure heart? We can understand it as purity of thought and spirit, honesty, and freedom from distracting thoughts. When our hearts are clean, we can experience God’s presence and see God’s work.

Let us imagine a scene: a little stream with water clear as a mirror. On its banks grow beautiful flowers and green grass, and sunlight falls on the water, sparkling with lovely light. This is a picture of a pure heart, representing an inner life full of goodness and God’s presence. When we keep a pure heart, our lives will be full of hope, love, and joy.

Yet we all know that in life we will always meet difficulties and challenges, and at times our hearts may be surrounded by sin, worry, or weariness. But when we become aware of these distractions and strive to shake them off, God’s grace flows into our lives. Like clearing a patch of grass, we need to remove the weeds so that the beautiful flowers and green grass can flourish again. In the same way, when we clear the distractions from our hearts, God’s glory and blessing will be shown again.

In our daily lives we can practice purity of heart by meeting God’s holy word, by prayer, and by repentance. As one saint said, “Prayer is the cleansing agent for the soul’s dirt.” When we connect with God and entrust ourselves into His hands, our hearts can be cleansed and we experience God’s presence.

Dear family, let us strive every day to keep a pure heart, and not let sin, worry, or weariness take over our hearts. When our hearts are clean, we can experience God’s presence and witness His wonderful works in our lives. May God bless us, so that we become pure in heart every day and enjoy the blessing of being valued and blessed by God.
a: Seek time alone
Find a quiet place to be alone with God, and let your heart become still to commune with Him. This can be at a fixed time, such as before you get up in the morning or before bed at night.
Review the day gone by

In your heart look back over what happened in the day, and ask whether your words and actions fully submitted to God’s will. Was there anything that displeased God? Honestly admit your mistakes and ask God for mercy.
Read and meditate on Scripture

Spend some time each day reading the Bible, and seek God’s word to guide your thoughts and actions. Whenever you read a verse that especially touches your heart, stop, meditate on it, and apply it to your own life.
Pray and praise
Bring the voice of your heart before God and pour out your joys, worries, and needs to Him. At the same time, do not forget to thank God and praise Him for His grace and lovingkindness to you.
Learn to keep watch

Pay attention to whether your thoughts, words, and actions line up with God’s will. When you find yourself troubled by negative emotions or speech, stop at once, ask God for help, and turn to God’s truth and promises.
Fellowship with spiritual companions
Find a spiritual companion or a small group to share your devotional experiences and challenges, encourage one another, pray for one another, and grow together.
Cultivate a thankful attitude

Learn to see God’s grace and blessing in everyday life, and give thanks to God for things great and small. Such an attitude helps us keep a clean heart that is watched over by God. By practicing purity of heart in daily life through these ways, we can draw closer to God and enjoy His abundant blessing. Whatever difficulty or challenge we face, we can meet it with a pure heart and receive strength and peace in God’s presence.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us this guide to action for living out a pure heart. We ask You to help us seek time alone, to be alone with You, so that our hearts become still to commune with You. Help us look back over the day gone by, honestly admit our mistakes, and ask You for forgiveness. Give us wisdom and strength to spend time each day reading the Bible and meditating on Your word. Teach us to pray and praise, so that we bring our joys, worries, and needs before You, and at the same time thank You for Your grace and lovingkindness to us. Remind us to keep watch over our thoughts, words, and actions, so that all of them are in line with Your will. Send the guidance of the Holy Spirit to help us grow and be built up in fellowship with spiritual companions. Cultivate in us a thankful attitude, so that we see Your grace and blessing in everyday life. By practicing purity of heart, may we draw closer to You and receive strength and peace in Your presence.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you receive strength and encouragement on the road of keeping a pure heart. As you witness God’s presence and blessing, may you bring others faith, hope, and love. Amen.

t: Blessed Are the Peacemakers
v: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
b: This passage reminds us that in this world full of conflict and strife, we are called to be peacemakers. Isn’t it hard to imagine getting along peacefully with people in a workplace conflict, or keeping harmony when settling a dispute at home? Yet God’s word tells us that if we can become peacemakers, we are blessed.

So what is a peacemaker? Such people treat others with a gentle and friendly attitude and respond to others’ needs and challenges with love. They are willing to communicate actively and to listen, and do not easily lose their temper or blame others. They know how to lay aside their own pride and personal interest to pursue the building of peace.

One day two neighbors had a quarrel. They were dissatisfied with each other’s behavior over a piece of land. They blamed each other, and their exchanges grew worse and worse. But one of them decided to change this situation. He took the initiative to approach the other and expressed understanding and respect for his point of view. This positive communication opened the door to dialogue, and in the end they reached a win-win agreement. Their peace not only settled the dispute, but also increased their friendship and trust.
Friends, when we live with others in love and peace, we are not merely mediators of conflict, but sons and daughters of God. We become a display of the image of God, showing His love and grace.

In daily life let us strive to be peacemakers and change situations of conflict and disharmony. Whether in the family, the workplace, or the community, we can solve problems with care and patience and build good relationships with love and peace.
ah: Here are some ways to practice peace and live in harmony with others in daily life, to help brothers and sisters build harmonious relationships:
a: Keep a peaceful mind

Regard peace as an inner state and let an atmosphere of peace radiate outward from within. Live in harmony with everyone as a child of God, and avoid the arising of negative emotions such as quarreling, resentment, and hatred.
Take the initiative to reconcile

When conflict or disagreement arises, do not let emotion rule, but take the initiative to approach the other person and seek a way to reconcile. Apologizing first, bearing with one another, and understanding the other’s point of view are important steps in building peace.
Develop communication skills

Good communication is the key to promoting peace. Learn to listen to others’ opinions and feelings and to express your own thoughts and needs. Building an open communication environment of mutual respect and acceptance can reduce misunderstanding and conflict.
Forgive and let go in good time

When others have hurt us, we need the courage to forgive and let go of past resentment. Forgiving does not mean forgetting, but letting go of resentment toward others and giving each other a chance to rebuild a harmonious relationship.
Show you are a child of God through your actions

Combine your life with your faith and become a true witness who shows you are a child of God. Treat others with love, compassion, and tolerance, bring Christian values into your daily life, and show the power of peace through your actions. Through these specific ways, we can practice peace in daily life and build harmonious relationships.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us guidance on building peace and living in harmony with others. We ask You to help us keep a peaceful mind, so that we may live in harmony with everyone like Your children. Give us a heart that takes the initiative to reconcile, and help us find ways to reconcile in conflict and disagreement.
