Help us develop good communication skills, so that we can listen to others’ opinions and feelings and express our own thoughts and needs. Give us the courage to forgive and let go of past resentment, so that we rebuild harmonious relationships with one another. Help us show that we are Your children through our actions, treating others with love, compassion, and tolerance, and showing Christian values in our daily lives. May we build peace among ourselves and pursue peace with a peaceful mind. We pray in the name of Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you become a peacemaker, bringing faith, hope, and love to the people around you. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Persecuted for Righteousness
v: Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
b: In this passage Jesus tells us that those who are persecuted because they pursue righteousness are blessed. They pay a price to guard the truth and stand on the side of justice. They may be rejected and ridiculed by the world, and even face danger to their lives, but God promises them the Kingdom of Heaven.

An ancient story tells of a brave warrior. He firmly believed in his tradition and faith, but under a cruel ruler he was watched and threatened. Yet he refused to yield and kept fighting for the truth, so that the evil ruler would not destroy their faith.

We may meet similar situations in our own lives. We may be tempted to lie, cheat, or go along with unjust behavior, but we must hold firmly to the truth and stand up for our faith. This may bring difficulty and persecution, but let us remember what God says to those persecuted for righteousness: “Blessed, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.”

When we face persecution, let us remember God’s promise. The Kingdom of Heaven is not only a hope for the future, but a spiritual treasure we can experience now. When the world rejects and ridicules us, we can find comfort and strength in the Kingdom of Heaven. God will protect us and supply what we need, so that we keep growing and flourishing in difficulty.

Let us follow this passage, hold fast to the truth, and fight bravely for righteousness. However great the adversity we face, believe that God will surely bless us, and that we will enjoy abundant grace and lovingkindness in the Kingdom of Heaven.
ah: To put Matthew 5:10 into practice in daily life, helping brothers and sisters live out their faith and experience God’s grace, we can follow these specific and effective ways:
a: Hold firm to your convictions

To endure suffering and persecution, we need firm convictions. We should build an intimate relationship with God so that we never give up our faith in Him. Through prayer, devotion, and reading the Bible, we can strengthen our faith in God and understand our place in the Kingdom of Heaven.
Live out righteousness

As believers, we are called to act justly. Wherever we are, we should hold to truth and integrity. When we face persecution and pressure, we should stand bravely on the side of justice and never compromise the truth. Through our words and deeds we can be a witness in others’ lives and show forth the kingdom of God.
Rejoice always

Though we suffer persecution, we can still keep our joy. We can seek God’s promises and comfort, and understand that He is with us in difficulty. Through thanksgiving and praise, we can turn our focus to God’s power and love.
Support one another

In adversity we need to support and encourage one another. As a Christian community, we should care for one another and stand with those who are persecuted for their faith. We can offer practical help, prayer, and support, so that they know they are not alone.
Pray

In the face of persecution and difficulty, we must have a firm and continual life of prayer. It is the most important way we connect with God, and through prayer we can seek God’s wisdom, strength, and grace to face hardship. Besides praying for ourselves, we should also pray for those who persecute us, asking God to show them grace and lead them into the Kingdom of Heaven. To put Matthew 5:10 into practice in daily life, we need to hold to our convictions, live out righteousness, keep rejoicing, support one another, and persist in prayer. These ways can help us walk with God in adversity and experience His grace and protection.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us the insight of Matthew 5:10, reminding us that we are blessed in suffering and persecution.
We ask You to help us hold firm to our convictions and not give up our faith in You in difficulty.
Let us live out righteousness, stand bravely on the side of justice, and be Your witnesses.
Give us joy, so that through thanksgiving and praise we turn our focus to Your power and love.
Help us support one another and stand with those who are persecuted, caring for and supporting one another.
Strengthen our life of prayer, so that we seek Your wisdom, strength, and grace to face difficulty.
Keep those who are persecuted, lead them into the Kingdom of Heaven, and show them grace.
We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you hold fast to the truth in hard times and fight for righteousness. May God’s grace and strength fill your life and make you a witness of light. Amen.

t: Blessed When Reviled for the Lord’s Sake
v: “Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
b: In this passage Jesus teaches us that when we are insulted, persecuted, and slandered by others because of our faith, we are blessed. This sounds a little strange. Why would we be blessed?

There was once a young Christian who lived out his faith very firmly. His colleagues mocked him and even shut him out because of his distinctive values and moral conduct. But the young Christian always stayed kind and loving, and never paid back evil words or harm.

One day his colleagues fell into trouble. They met difficulties in life, but no one was willing to help them. The young Christian took the initiative to reach out, helped them solve their problems, and gave them comfort and support. His colleagues were moved by his good deeds and reconsidered their view of him.

This story tells us that when we respond to others’ insults and persecution with kindness and love, we can change their hearts. When we face difficulty and hurt with a positive attitude, we not only gain inner peace ourselves, but can also influence others’ lives.

So when we are insulted, persecuted, and slandered because of our faith, let us respond with the love of Jesus. Let us be like that young Christian and change the people around us with good deeds and love. For we know that in the end it is God’s truth and love that will overcome all malice and falsehood.
a: Accept insults and persecution

When others insult, persecute, or slander us because of our faith, we should accept it with a peaceful mind. This is because we know that God has given us grace, so that we are able to endure these difficulties.
Hold to the truth
When we face persecution, we should hold to the truth we believe. However the world changes, God’s truth never changes. We should keep the truth in our hearts and apply it in our daily lives.
Keep loving

We should keep love for those who act with malice toward us. It is not easy, but this is exactly where Christians differ from the world. When we bring love into adversity, we can be a witness of light and show others God’s love.
Pray and depend on God

When we face adversity, we should learn to depend on God and find strength and wisdom through prayer. Prayer is an important way of connecting with God, and it helps us receive support and guidance in difficulty.
Lead by example

Carry the attitudes and values the Lord taught through your own conduct and be an example to others. When we show a character different from the world in our daily lives, we have the opportunity to influence others’ lives.
Seek fellowship and support

On the journey of faith we need to support one another and have fellowship. Find a spiritual family or small group, share the challenges of faith and life with other Christians, and support one another.
Do not forget God’s promises

When we face insults and persecution, we should not forget God’s promises. God has assured us that He is with us, and that His grace and power are enough for any difficulty. By practicing these ways, we can better live out our identity as Christians in daily life and face the troubles we meet with faith, hope, and love.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us blessing and strength to face insults and persecution. We ask You to give us firm faith, so that we hold to the truth and keep loving in difficulty. Teach us to depend on Your strength in prayer and to seek wisdom. Help us lead by example and be Your witnesses of light. Lead us to find fellowship and support, and remind us not to forget Your promises. May we face every difficulty with faith, hope, and love. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you keep faith and hope in difficulty and respond to others’ malice with love. May you have a positive influence on the lives of others and bring them true blessing. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Who See the Lord
v: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
b: In this passage the Lord Jesus tells us that we are blessed because we can see and hear. Seeing and hearing here mean not only physical perception, but being able to grasp spiritual truth and God’s will.

Imagine a blind man who has never been able to see the beauty and wonder of the world. Then suddenly he receives sight. He sees the gold of sunlight spilling over the earth, he sees flowers blooming and little birds in flight, and he feels a joy that moves him to the depths of his soul. In the same way, when we can see God’s truth, we can feel a joy and peace that the world cannot give.

Or imagine a deaf man who cannot hear people’s words or the melody of music. Then suddenly he can hear. He hears his friends’ greetings and laughter, and he hears the happiness music brings. In the same way, when we can hear God’s voice, we can feel a stillness and comfort that the world cannot provide.

This passage reminds us that we are not merely blessed, but very blessed! We have eyes to see what God is doing around us, and ears to hear God’s voice to us. This is a priceless grace and blessing, and we should be thankful for it and treasure it.

Let us use these blessed eyes to see the wonder of God in our lives, and to see His grace and guidance every day. Let us use these blessed ears to hear God’s words to us, and to hear His mercy and encouragement. May such eyes and ears help us know God more deeply and take hold of His plan for our lives.
a: Open your heart
Lay aside your own prejudice and stubborn views, and let God’s word and work enter your heart.
Focus on God’s word
Give time and attention to reading the Bible and thinking carefully about its message. Only then can we truly understand God’s heart and will.
Pray sincerely
Build a close relationship with God and entrust your thoughts, feelings, and needs to Him. In this way we can experience His guidance and response.
Stay sensitive
Pay attention to what God is doing and saying around us, including the messages He conveys to us through people, nature, and experience.
Cultivate a thankful heart
Thank God for everything He gives us in life, whether good or not so smooth. In this way we can appreciate His grace and blessing even more.
Share God’s love
Use words of inspiration and encouragement to help others see what God is doing, and show Christ’s love and mercy in your life.
Take action

Do not only hear the message, but put God’s word into practice. Through action we can truly experience God’s blessing and response. These ways can help us practice and personally experience God’s blessing in daily life. When we stay sensitive and respond keenly to God’s leading, we can know Him more deeply and let His love and grace flow out to influence and benefit the people around us.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
Thank You for giving us the blessing of eyes that see You and ears that hear You. We ask You to give us an open heart, so that Your word and work enter our lives. Help us focus on reading the Bible and think carefully about its message, to truly understand Your heart and will. Build a close relationship with us, so that our prayers are sincere and powerful. Teach us to stay sensitive and to notice what You are doing and saying around us. Inspire us to cultivate a thankful heart and thank You for all You have given. Help us share Your love, encouraging and helping others to see what You are doing. Help us not only to hear the message but to put Your word into practice. Shape us into witnesses of Your heart, to influence and benefit the people around us. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you use these blessed eyes every day to see God’s work and goodness, and these blessed ears every day to hear God’s voice and guidance. Amen.

t: Hearing and Keeping the Word Is More Blessed
v: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
b: This passage reminds us that merely hearing the word is not enough. What matters more is keeping God’s word after we hear it. We can compare this keeping to eating. We may look at delicious food, but if we do not eat it, our strength and health cannot improve. In the same way, we need to turn God’s word into action in order to truly feel its blessing and power.

In a certain city there was a young man named Joseph who longed for success and wealth. He worked hard, learned new skills, and achieved great things in his career. But though he seemed successful on the outside, inside he felt empty and unsatisfied.

Then one day he happened to hear a pastor preach and quote this passage. The pastor told everyone that true blessing is not found in pursuing worldly achievement but in obeying God’s word and keeping His teaching.

This was a turning point in Joseph’s thinking. He began to spend more time reading the Bible, attending church gatherings, and sharing with spiritual companions. He gradually understood that true blessing is to build an intimate relationship with God and live out Christian values.

This story tells us that when we lay down the pursuit of worldly glory and wealth and listen wholeheartedly to God’s word, we will find inner peace and satisfaction. Though the world may not understand why we hold to our faith, when we walk on the spiritual road we will experience true blessing.
So let us sincerely listen to God’s word every day and strive to keep His teaching. When we live in His will, we will feel the power of faith, hope, and love flowing in our lives.
a: Read the Bible daily
Set aside time each morning or evening to read the Bible. This will help us understand God’s way better and let God’s word become the guide for our lives.
Meditate and apply
Beyond reading, we need to quiet our hearts, meditate on God’s word, and think about how to apply it in our own lives. Doing so helps us understand God’s heart more deeply and practice His way.
Pray
Talk with God several times a day and bring our wishes and troubles before Him. Through prayer we can touch God’s heart and receive strength and wisdom to keep His word.
Build fellowship
Join a church or small group and study and share God’s word together with other Christians. Such fellowship lets us encourage and remind one another and practice God’s way in daily life.
Humble obedience
We must not only hear God’s word but keep His teaching. This means being willing to lay down our own opinions and rights, to submit to God’s will, and to do what pleases Him.
Reflect and review
Regularly reflect on our conduct and attitudes and review whether there is anywhere we have strayed from God’s word. Doing so helps us examine and correct our mistakes and keep growing.
Seek help

If we meet difficulty or challenge in putting God’s word into practice, we should not be afraid to ask other mature Christians for help and guidance. They can give us wisdom and support and walk with us as we grow. When we strive each day to hear God’s word and apply it in our lives, we will experience God’s blessing and guidance. Let us work together to practice God’s word and become blessed people who keep God’s way.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, I thank You for giving us God’s word to guide our lives. We ask You to help us read, meditate on, and apply Your word every day. Let us often talk with You and seek Your heart in prayer. Lead us to become a fellowship that studies and shares together with other Christians. Make us humble and obedient, laying down our own opinions and rights and keeping Your teaching. Help us keep growing through reflection and review, and seek help in difficulty. Bless us, so that we become blessed people who keep God’s way. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you listen to God’s word with a humble heart every day. May you experience true blessing as you keep His teaching, and bring faith, hope, and love to those around you. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Who Watch and Wait
v: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.
b: This passage reminds us to keep watching and waiting at all times, because when the master returns and finds us watchful servants, we will be blessed. This is also God’s call to us, to be ready at any time to welcome His coming.

Watching and waiting refers not only to the second coming of the Lord Jesus, but also to every moment of our fellowship with God in our lives. We must keep our spirits keen and stay in contact with God at all times, so that we can receive His guidance and revelation. When we watch and wait, God delights to walk with us and rewards us with spiritual food and grace.

A story tells of a wealthy merchant who had many servants working on his estate. The merchant often traveled on business, but he was very strict about his servants’ work. One day the merchant suddenly returned to the estate earlier than expected and saw one of the servants working diligently, without any slackness. The merchant was pleased by his watchfulness and invited him to sit down and eat together. Because of his watchfulness, this servant received his master’s praise and blessing.

This story tells us that we should stay watchful at all times as we wait for the master to come. In our lives the master stands for Jesus Christ, who may come anytime and anywhere, whether in our workplace, our home, or our community. When we watchfully carry out our responsibilities and are full of love and care for others, we will be like that watchful servant and receive the master’s blessing and praise.

In this busy modern society, we easily get lost in the small details of life and overlook the master’s coming. But if we stay watchful at all times, pay attention to the needs around us, and are always ready to serve others, we will feel the master’s presence and blessing.

Dear friends, let us remember the teaching of this passage every day and stay watchful and glad to serve. When we meet the challenges of life with faith, hope, and love, we will be servants who please the master, and at His appointed time He will surely bless us. In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you receive abundant blessing as you watch and wait.
a: Develop the habit of devotion
Spend some time with God every day in Bible reading, prayer, and meditation, to keep your spirit clear and sensitive.
Hold on to faith
Believe the promise of the Lord Jesus and know that He will surely come again. Do not lose faith because of the troubles and trials of the world, but keep waiting for the Lord’s return.
Prepare every day

Keep good character and conduct at all times, so that improper behavior does not cause you to miss the Lord’s return. Treat others with love and integrity, and do not indulge yourself in the temptation of sin.
Serve others
Serve others with a humble heart and show Christ’s love and care in daily life. Do not only wait for the Lord Jesus to return, but pass His love on to others.
Plan ahead
Plan and take appropriate action in preparation for the Lord’s coming. This may include arranging your family, work, and service affairs so that you are prepared in every respect.
Do not be led astray by the world
Do not be troubled by the temptations and worries of the world, but focus on the spiritual life and on waiting for the Lord’s return. Do not let material wealth become a burden to your soul.
Encourage one another

Share this hope with other brothers and sisters, and encourage, support, and pray for one another. Build an environment of mutual care and shared growth in the fellowship and the church. Through these practical and effective ways, we can practice watching and waiting in daily life, so that when the Lord Jesus comes again we can enjoy His blessing and glory. Whatever our present situation, let us hold firm in faith, keep waiting, and strive to pass Christ’s love on to the people around us.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, we thank You for Your promise and grace. We ask You to help us develop the habit of devotion every day and keep our spirits clear and sensitive. Strengthen our faith, so that we wait wholeheartedly for Your return. Give us wisdom, so that we prepare ourselves at all times, show Christ’s love, and serve others. Protect us from being led astray by the world, so that we focus on the spiritual life. Strengthen our fellowship and care, as we encourage and support one another. Lord, may we not lose hope as we wait, and become witnesses to Your blessing and glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you receive abundant blessing as you watch and wait. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Who Know and Do
v: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
b: Knowledge itself is precious, but only when knowledge is turned into action can it truly bring blessing. Many people long for a good life, but often stay at the level of longing and take no action to carry it out. Yet the Bible tells us that only by doing can we receive true blessing.

There was a farmer who longed to have fields with a rich harvest, but he only sat at home dreaming of an abundant crop. He knew he needed to plow, irrigate, and wait patiently, but he was unwilling to put in the hard labor. In the end, when harvest season came, his fields were empty.
This story tells us that merely knowing is not enough to change our lives. We must act and put into practice the truth we know. Every day God gives us countless opportunities to walk in His ways.

This kind of doing applies not only to the spiritual life, but also to our daily lives. For example, in our interactions with others, we can choose to act with love and forgiveness and build harmonious relationships. At work, we can put in effort and creativity and pursue excellence and success. These actions are all based on the truth we know, and not merely left in the mind.
Dear family, let us remember that God gives us knowledge and wisdom and expects us to turn them into action. Only when we do can we truly experience His blessing and joy.
a: Understand God’s will
Spend time every day reading the Bible and seeking God’s will and guidance. In this way we can know more clearly how God wants us to live.
Live out your faith in truth

It is not enough to have knowledge; we must put it into practice. We need to live out our identity as Christians with sincerity and devotion, so that our actions and words are in line with God’s will.
Build the right values
There are many temptations and deceptions in the world that easily make us lose our way. Yet by walking with God we can establish spiritual values, so that we can make wise choices in daily life.
Serve others
According to the teaching of Jesus, we should serve others with love. In daily life we can care about others’ needs, help others, and give support and encouragement, to show the love of Christ.
Lead others to know God

We can lead others to know God by sharing our faith and experience. This lets others receive the benefit of the gospel, and it is also one specific way of practicing “blessed are you if you do them.” These are ways we practice this truth in daily life. As we walk firmly on this road, we will draw nearer to God and build a deeper relationship with Him. At the same time, our conduct and example will influence those around us and bring them hope, comfort, and God’s love.
pr:
Dear Heavenly Father,
We ask You to give us understanding of Your way, and to live out our faith through real action.
Help us build the right values, be set apart from the world, and serve others in love.
Guide us, so that we become instruments for leading others to know God.
May we draw nearer to You on the road of “blessed are you if you do them,” and become witnesses of hope, comfort, and God’s love to the people around us.
We ask in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you be bold every day to do God’s will, and live out faith, hope, and love both in the spiritual life and in daily life. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Who Believe Without Seeing
v: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.”
b: In this passage Jesus spoke these words to his disciple Thomas. At that time Thomas was not with the other disciples on that Sunday after Jesus was crucified when they saw the risen Jesus, and he doubted what the other disciples had seen and heard. But when Jesus appeared before him and let him touch the nail-scarred hands and the pierced side, Thomas’s doubt turned into faith.

This passage tells us that some people need actual evidence in order to believe in Jesus’ resurrection, while others have firm faith before they have seen. Those who believe without seeing are full of blessing, because they do not need verification by the eye to hold firm to Jesus’ resurrection.

This also reminds us of a story about a man named Joseph. Joseph was a poor farmer who worked his land by prayer and faith. Though the people around him laughed at him for believing in things unseen, Joseph did not give up. One day a long drought struck, the crops withered, and people lost hope. Yet Joseph still held on to God’s word, kept praying, and planted his seeds.

When everyone had lost confidence in Joseph, a miracle happened. Rain fell abundantly, the crops were watered, and Joseph’s land became the most fertile of all. His faith and hope brought a harvest, and he became an example to the people around him.

This story tells us that even in adversity we should keep faith and hope. Just as Thomas needed to see the signs of Jesus in order to believe, Joseph needed to wait for the rain to see the result of the harvest. But whether or not we see, as long as we firmly believe God’s promise, His blessing will come to us.

I want to tell you, let us not lose faith when we face difficulty and challenge. Even if we have not yet seen God’s blessing, let us believe His word, His grace, and His promise. God’s plan is good and perfect, and He will never let us down.
ah: We can practice the truth of this passage in daily life in the following ways:
a: Deepen your knowledge of Jesus

Building an intimate relationship with God is the key to practicing this passage. Through quiet prayer and Bible reading each day, we can understand Jesus’ teaching and His work in our lives more deeply.
Act in faith

This is an important step in believing when we do not see. We can show our faith in God in daily life, for example by serving others, being kind to others, and keeping God’s commandments. Such actions show our faith in God and let us receive blessing in practice.
Share your faith
When others see our way of life and our faith in God, they may also be inspired. By sharing our faith experience and the core values of our faith with others, we can lead them into God’s light.
Rely on the Spirit’s guidance

The Holy Spirit is our Helper and Guide, and He can help us practice the truth of this passage in daily life. We can rely on the Spirit’s guidance at all times, letting His wisdom and strength help us believe in God even when we do not see.
Keep learning and growing

Faith is a process of continual development. We can attend church gatherings, join small groups, or read spiritual books to keep learning and growing, and practice our faith in God in daily life. Through these practical and effective ways, we can practice the truth of this passage in daily life. In this way we can receive blessing and be a blessing and encouragement to others.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the blessing of faith. We ask You to help us trust You not only when we see, but to believe firmly even when we do not see. Guide us to deepen our relationship with Jesus, so that our daily lives show our faith in You. Help us, through action, to serve others and be faithful to Your commandments, and be a blessing and encouragement to others. May the wisdom and strength of the Holy Spirit lead us, so that in continual learning and growth we believe in You more firmly. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you find strength in faith, comfort in hope, and warmth in love. May God’s blessing keep coming upon your life. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One Who Does Not Condemn Himself
v: Do you have faith? Have it to yourself before God. Happy is he who doesn’t judge himself in that which he approves.
b: In this passage Paul tells us that when we have faith, we should hold on to that faith before God. If we do not condemn ourselves in what we believe is right, that is a blessed state.

In our lives, there are times when we make mistakes or unwise choices, and then we may blame ourselves and regret. But this passage reminds us that when we have real faith and trust God’s guidance and grace, we can let go of past faults and stop blaming ourselves.

There was a farmer who worked hard every day, plowing his fields and caring for his plants as they grew. One day he carelessly made a mistake and put the wrong chemical fertilizer on his crops. He blamed himself and regretted it deeply, because he knew this mistake could have bad consequences for his harvest.

Yet the farmer did not let self-blame and regret bind his heart. Instead, he confidently handed the problem to God. He believed that God’s grace and power could make up for his mistake. He began to tend each crop with love and patience, and went on caring for his farm.

In the end, the farmer was amazed to find that although he had made a mistake, the other crops grew more lush than expected. He understood that this was a display of God’s grace and guidance at work. He no longer blamed himself, but gave thanks for God’s grace and wonderful works.

Dear family, there may be times in our lives when we make mistakes, but let us remember the truth this passage teaches. When we have real faith and trust God’s grace and guidance, we can let go of self-blame and regret. Instead, we can go forward by faith, believing that God will show His wonderful works through our mistakes.
ah: Here are ways to put this passage into practice in daily life:
a: Trust God
Believe firmly in God’s existence and His plan for you. Then you can let go of self-blame, because you know an almighty Heavenly Father is in charge of your life.
Learn from your mistakes
When you make a mistake or meet failure, do not blame yourself or be discouraged, but treat these as opportunities to learn and grow. Accept your shortcomings and look for ways to improve.
Forgive yourself
Do not drag past mistakes and faults into the present. Learn to forgive yourself and look forward. Then you can truly set yourself free and keep going in God’s grace.
Seek God’s will

When making decisions, do not rely only on your own wisdom and ability, but seek God’s will. By praying and listening to the Holy Spirit’s guidance, you will be more certain that what you choose is in line with God’s heart.
Praise and thanksgiving

Keep a thankful heart at all times and praise God for all He has given. Through praise and thanksgiving, you can learn to see the miracles and grace in your own life and be full of confidence. Thank You to the Holy Spirit for leading us to understand the truth and live by it. May God bless you!
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us today’s reminder from Your word. We ask You to help us put these action guides into practice in daily life. Help us trust You, learn from our mistakes, forgive ourselves, seek Your will, and always praise and give thanks. May God’s peace and blessing fill our lives. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: when you face self-blame and regret, may you confidently trust God’s grace and guidance. May you gain faith, hope, and love, and use this blessing to inspire and move others. Amen.

t: It Is More Blessed to Give Than to Receive
v: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”
b: This passage reminds us of our mission and values as Christians. We follow Paul, as Paul followed Jesus. We are to be an example to others by our conduct. We should be willing to labor to help the weak, and seize every opportunity to give and help others. In this world, many people need help, care, and encouragement, and we should gladly commit ourselves and do our best to support them. Such giving can not only change others’ lives, but will also bring us greater blessing.

A fisherman cast his nets in the bitter cold wind. He toiled hard without complaint, because he knew that once he caught fish, his family would have enough to eat and he could help others in need. In the same way, when we use our time, ability, and resources to help others, we not only benefit them, but also receive abundant blessing ourselves.

A rich man saw a beggar shivering with cold and gave him a thick coat. But a few days later the rich man saw the beggar in the slums, giving that thick coat to others who needed it more. The rich man was deeply moved, and he understood the true meaning of “it is more blessed to give than to receive.” For while we give, we also receive more love and blessing.

In life we often focus only on pursuing our own interests and enjoyment, and overlook the people around us who need help. But when we learn, like the Lord Jesus, to help the weak, we find that our souls are nourished and our lives become richer.

Let us ask ourselves each day: “Did I help the weak today? Did I pour out grace on someone in need today?” When we bring an attitude of caring for and loving others into our lives, we can truly experience the joy and satisfaction that it is more blessed to give than to receive.
ah: “Dear family, peace to you. Let us follow the action guide of today’s Soul Snack together.” Today’s passage reminds us that we should help the weak by setting an example. Here are some practical and effective ways to help us put this principle into practice in daily life:
a: Look for opportunities

Stay sensitive and alert, and notice people around you who need help. It may be a friend who is physically weak, or a colleague who is emotionally hurting. Whatever the situation, we should look for opportunities to reach out a hand.
Labor and give

Helping others takes time and effort, and we must be willing to labor to help them. It may be keeping company with a lonely elder, or helping by giving support and encouragement. Whatever the way, we should give with love.
Give care

Besides concrete actions, we can also help the weak with an attitude of care. It can be a warm smile, a word of encouragement, or a small gift. We can express our concern and love for them in caring ways.
Remember the words of the Lord Jesus

The Lord Jesus told us, “It is more blessed to give than to receive,” reminding us to live with an attitude of serving others. When we remember this saying and put it into practice, we will have more joy and peace. Thank You to the Holy Spirit for leading us to understand the truth and live by it. May God bless you!
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us today to help the weak with an attitude that gives more than it receives. We ask You to give us a sensitive and alert heart, so that we can notice those around us who are in need. Give us a heart that labors, and may we be willing to give time and effort to help them. Give us a warm and caring heart, so that we can express our concern and love for them in caring ways. Lord, let us always remember the words of the Lord Jesus and live with a heart to serve others. Help us put this principle into practice in daily life in real and effective ways, and let us be examples to one another. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you be a helper of the weak every day, and receive abundant blessing from it. Amen.

t: Blessed Is the One Who Endures Temptation
v: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.
b: In our lives temptation is an unavoidable part. Whether we face allurement, difficulty, or setback, we will meet temptation in various forms. Yet this passage tells us that when we face temptation with firm faith and hope, we are blessed.

A young carpenter worked hard to build beautiful houses for people to live in. But one day he met a very difficult project, and he was not sure he could complete it. Yet he did not give up. Instead, he actively faced the temptation of discouragement and fear, looking forward to succeeding through the test and growing in life. At last he successfully completed this hard project and won people’s praise and respect.

This story tells us that when we endure temptation, we not only overcome difficulty but also grow in it. Temptation can be an opportunity to test our faith, perseverance, and character. Like the carpenter, through effort and continual struggle we can overcome difficulties and in the end receive the crown of life that belongs to us.

In life we face all kinds of trials. It may be pressure at work, challenges in relationships, or the trouble of health problems. But when we face these temptations with faith and hope, we will be able to see God’s great power and grace at work in our lives.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you stand firm in faith, hold hope in your heart when you face temptation, and receive the crown of life through trials. Amen.
No. 434 Soul Snack Action Guide

t: Blessed Are Those Who Endure
v: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
b: In our lives we often meet all kinds of challenges and difficulties, and at such times we need endurance. But endurance is not easy. It takes tenacious faith and unrelenting effort. Like Job, who went through great suffering but endured and always kept his faith in God. In the end God blessed him abundantly, not only with material blessing, but even more with spiritual satisfaction and joy.

In our own lives we also need to learn endurance. When we face challenges and adversity, let us not give up or yield easily. Believe that God will lead us through the difficulty and give us strength and wisdom to face everything. Endurance is a virtue. It lets us keep growing and advancing, and it also shows our faith in and dependence on God.

Sometimes we may feel that endurance is too hard, and we may feel disappointed and hopeless. But we must remember that God is full of compassion. He watches over us, and when we are most helpless He gives us strength and comfort. His love and grace are always with us, and whatever difficulty or trial we face, we can believe that He will richly bless us in the end.

Let us learn the endurance of Job and stand firm on God’s promises and truth. However many difficulties and challenges we face, let us look to the Lord’s lovingkindness and compassion and keep faith and hope. For those who endure are blessed, and they will experience God’s limitless grace and blessing.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you show Job’s endurance and faith in every difficulty. May you find comfort and strength in God’s lovingkindness and compassion. May your life be filled with God’s blessing and become a witness to His love. Amen.
No. 435 Soul Snack Action Guide. James 5:11: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the Lord’s end, that the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

t: Blessed to Suffer for Righteousness
v: But even if you should suffer for righteousness’ sake, you are blessed. “Don’t fear what they fear, neither be troubled.”
b: In this passage God tells us that suffering for the sake of righteousness is worthwhile, and that we are blessed. This may confuse us, because when we think of suffering and pain, we do not usually think of ourselves as blessed.
A young man named David worked hard, but he was often bullied and mocked by his colleagues. He felt very discouraged and helpless, and sometimes even wanted to give up.

Yet David was a Christian of firm faith, and he knew that God’s word promises we are blessed when we suffer for righteousness. So he began to call on God, asking Him for strength and wisdom to deal with these difficulties. Every morning he entrusted himself fully to the Lord and went on facing the challenges steadfastly.

Although David suffered for a long time, he was never shaken by his colleagues’ threats. On the contrary, his attitude and conduct had a positive influence. In the face of sneers and sarcasm, he always responded with love and tolerance. Slowly his colleagues noticed the change in David, and they began to hold him in respect.

In the end David became a leader in the team, and his colleagues came to him for help and guidance. His life became their witness, because he faced difficulty with an attitude of faith and hope and showed God’s love.

This story tells us that it is a blessing to suffer for righteousness. When we meet adversity in life, we can respond with an attitude of faith and hope. This can change not only our own lives but also the lives of those around us.

So let us not fear people’s threats or be troubled. When we suffer for righteousness, we are blessed, because God is surely with us in these sufferings and gives us strength and wisdom to overcome everything.
ah: In daily life we often meet all kinds of difficulties and challenges. But this passage reminds us that when we suffer for righteousness, we are blessed. Now let us see together how to put this truth into practice in daily life.
a: Hold to your faith
Whatever difficulty we meet, we should hold to our faith and not let outside pressure and threats shake us. Trust God’s grace and strength, and stand firmly on His truth.
Be glad to help

When we see others suffering in hardship, we should be glad to reach out a hand and give help and support. This reflects God’s love and care, and it also lives out the truth of the gospel in the experience of suffering for righteousness.
Stay calm

However great the difficulties and challenges we meet in life, we should learn to keep inner calm and peace. This does not mean ignoring problems or escaping reality, but relying on God’s strength and wisdom in difficulty and seeking solutions.
Learn to forgive

When others treat us unfairly or hurt us, we need to learn to forgive. Following the example of Jesus Christ, we respond with love and tolerance, so that even as we suffer for righteousness we show God’s grace and love.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us today that it is a blessing to suffer for righteousness. Give us firm faith, so that we do not bend in adversity. Help us be glad to help, and with love and care to help those who are in suffering. Give us a calm heart, so that in difficulty we look to Your strength. We also ask You to give us the ability to forgive those who have hurt us. May we live out Your gospel with such an attitude, and become blessed people who suffer for righteousness. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: when you suffer for righteousness, may you feel God’s presence and protection. May your faith keep growing, and may your life become His witness. Amen.

t: Blessed to Be Insulted for the Lord
v: If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you. On their part he is blasphemed, but on your part he is glorified.
b: This passage reminds us that when we are insulted for the name of Christ, we are blessed. Yes, the world may mock our faith, and may not understand why we hold on to belief in God. But when we hold to our faith in difficulty, the Spirit of God’s glory rests on us.

A young Christian named Mingren was laughed at by his classmates at school because he was unwilling to join activities that conflicted with his moral values. He held to his faith and chose not to take part in things that did not accord with God’s will. Although he was laughed at and looked down on by his classmates, he did not yield to the pressure, because he knew his faith was real and valuable.

This story tells us that when we hold to the truth, even if we are mocked and reviled, we are still blessed. We can show God’s glory in difficulty, and let people see our endurance, perseverance, and love.

Now let us bring the truth of this passage into our daily lives. Perhaps in your workplace or at school you may face pressure that conflicts with your faith. But do not let the world’s views affect your faith. Remember that when you are insulted for Christ, you are blessed. The Spirit of God’s glory rests on you, which enables you to respond with love, joy, and peace.
a: Stay faithful to Christ
On every occasion and whatever the difficulty, we should hold to our loyalty to Christ and not give up our faith in order to escape insults.
Respond with love
When we are insulted, we should learn to respond with love, forgive one another, and show the love of Christ. Such a response shows our loyalty to Christ and can also move others.
Live a glorious life
The Spirit of glory and of God rests on us, which is a precious gift. We should guard our words and conduct and bear witness to God’s glory with a life of light.
Hold firm in faith
When we suffer insults, we should hold firm in faith and know that this is an opportunity for our faith to be tested. Trust God’s plan in it, and seek His strength and wisdom.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us the insight of this passage. We ask You to help us put these action guides into practice in daily life: not to give up the name of Christ easily, to respond to insults with love, to live a glorious life, and to hold firm in faith. Send Your Spirit to keep adding to our strength and wisdom, so that we become light and salt that show Your glory. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you hold to your faith in any circumstance and stand unyielding on the truth. May the Spirit of God’s glory rest on you, making you a light and salt that leads others. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Who Die in the Lord
v: I heard a voice from heaven saying, “Write, ‘Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.’” “Yes,” says the Spirit, “that they may rest from their labors, for their works follow with them.”
b: The Spirit says, “Yes, that they may rest from their labors; for their works follow with them.”

This passage reminds us that those in Christ are blessed, even though they have died. A voice comes from heaven and proclaims to us: those who die in the Lord are blessed! They have laid down their toil, and the work they have done has produced abundant fruit.

We can imagine a believer who served the Lord all his life and poured out much effort and labor. Yet after he has died, we see that his work was not in vain but continues to bring blessing and change. The seeds he sowed, the love and truth he spread, still take root and sprout after he is gone, carrying on the kingdom of God.

This passage also reminds us that death is not the end, but a turning point. When we die with Christ, we are actually experiencing the beginning of new life. Just as a seed must die before it can sprout and grow, we also need to lay down self and worldly desires and let Christ’s life grow within us.

So we can find hope and comfort in death. We know that death is only the door to eternity, and that we will be with the Lord and enjoy blessing forever. Death is no longer our enemy, but an opportunity in the kingdom of God.

So let us receive this gospel truth in faith and experience the Lord’s work in our lives. Even though death may bring grief and loss, we can believe that those who have died in the Lord have already gained true victory and blessing.
a: Know the Lord Jesus

Bring the Lord Jesus into your life, to be your personal Savior and Lord. Build an intimate relationship with the Lord and deepen your knowledge and love of Him through prayer and meditation on God’s word.
Learn to entrust your life to the Lord

Understand that dying in the Lord is not the end of the spiritual life but the beginning of entering eternal glory. Learn to entrust your life fully to the Lord, let go of control, and trust that He has the best plan and purpose.
Serve in faith

By faith, in the direction the Lord points out, throw yourself actively into the work of His kingdom. Use your talents and resources for the glory of God, serve His people, and strive to build the kingdom of God.
Live out hope and joy

Understand that it is a blessing to die in the Lord, and that we can have eternal hope and joy. Whether in difficulty or challenge, face it with faith and a joyful heart, because we know our future is to be with the Lord.
Share the Lord’s love and salvation

Share the Lord’s love and salvation with others and be a witness for God. Through words and conduct, show the Lord’s grace and truth, and lead more people to know the Lord Jesus and experience His redemption.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this beautiful passage, which reminds us that it is a blessing to die in the Lord. We ask You to help us know the Lord Jesus and entrust our lives fully to Him. Help us live out this gospel with faith and a joyful heart, and share the Lord’s love and salvation with others. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen!
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you live out this gospel truth in faith and walk with the Lord into eternity. Amen.

t: Blessed Are Those Invited to the Feast
v: He said to me, “Write, ‘Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb.’” He said to me, “These are true words of God.”
b: In our lives we are often invited to all kinds of gatherings and events. Sometimes we may feel excited and expectant, but few things can be more exciting and thrilling than being invited to a wedding feast.

Imagine that you receive an exquisite invitation to a grand wedding. It is a wedding feast hosted personally by the Heavenly Father for His Son, the Lamb of God, the Lord Jesus. It is a great occasion that symbolizes the spiritual marriage between God and us. It is an occasion that shows God’s abundant grace and lovingkindness.

Such an invitation fills us with immense joy and honor. We know that at this feast we will celebrate together with angels, saints, and all believers. It will be a celebration full of joy, music, food, and peace.

This picture reminds us that God’s love and kindness are immeasurably deep. He not only invites us to take part in His kingdom, but has also prepared an abundant feast for us. He looks forward to our coming and to celebrating with us.

On the journey of our lives, we may sometimes face difficulties and challenges. We may feel tired, disappointed, even lost. But when we recall the joy and glory of being invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb, it will give us strength and courage.

So let us remember this true message every day: all who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb are blessed! Whatever our life is like, whatever challenges we face, we know that God’s love and grace will lead us through everything.

Let us keep connecting with God and go forward in faith in His love. He has invited us to share in His kingdom, His joy and glory. May this message take deep root in our lives and bring us endless faith, hope, and love.
a: Welcome each day with a thankful heart
Each morning, take five minutes to think about the blessings you have and thank God. Whether it is health, family, work, or anything else, remember to place these blessings within God’s blessing.
Cultivate and pass on love

In daily life, look for opportunities to help others and give love and support. Whether helping those in need or giving encouragement and affirmation to those around you, this is our response to God’s love.
Keep a joyful heart

Even in difficulty and trial, we should keep a joyful spirit. This is not only an expression of faith, but also a way of showing the world God’s love and power. Each morning when you get up, begin the new day with a happy gesture or laughter.
Wait for the wedding supper of the Lamb with hope

We should keep reminding ourselves of the hope of eternal life. Though present troubles may make us feel despair, we should firmly believe that at the wedding supper of the Lamb we will receive complete joy and satisfaction.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for the action guide You have reminded us to follow today. We ask You to help us welcome each day with a thankful heart, cultivate and pass on love, keep a joyful heart, and wait with hope for the wedding supper of the Lamb. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you experience God’s true words and keep going forward in the joy of being invited in the future to the wedding supper of the Lamb. Amen.

t: Blessed to Share in the Resurrection
v: Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection. Over these, the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and will reign with him one thousand years.
b: This passage reminds us how blessed are those who have a part in the first resurrection! Because they have been raised with Christ, they are made holy and become priests of God and of Christ, reigning with Christ in the kingdom of the thousand years.

A young girl named Vivian had gone through many misfortunes in her life. Her parents died when she was very young, and so she knew a lonely, helpless childhood. After Vivian grew up, she married an abusive husband, and her life fell into hardship. She felt hopeless and helpless and did not know how to escape this plight.

But when Vivian met Jesus Christ, everything changed. She understood the meaning of the Bible’s promise, “Blessed is he who has a part in the first resurrection.” Through her connection with Christ, she received the hope and strength of new life. Vivian began to seek God’s will, and she grasped that through Christ she could be more than a conqueror in everything, and she came to hold the promise that in the future she would sit on Christ’s throne and reign with Christ.

In the kingdom of God, Vivian became a royal priest, serving God and Christ. She used her talents and love to care for those who suffer, bringing them grace and blessing. She became an example that everyone followed and respected. Vivian experienced the power of resurrection, and her life was made new, full of God’s grace and glory.

This story tells us that when we face hardship, we need not despair. Because of our connection with Christ, we can experience being raised with the Lord and receiving new life. By letting Christ reign in our new life, we have the power to bring others true hope and love. Whatever our circumstances, God’s grace and glory are with us forever.

So let us keep this truth in mind every day and meet the challenges of life with faith, hope, and love. Believe that God has prepared abundant blessing for us, and that together with Christ we build the glory of the kingdom of God.
ah: Here are several specific ways to help brothers and sisters put today’s passage into practice in daily life:
a: Stay holy
Seek God’s face, build an intimate relationship with God, and keep God’s commandments. This can be done through daily quiet time, reading Scripture, prayer, and repentance.
Be a priest of Christ
Follow the pattern of Christ and live with love, forgiveness, and a heart to serve others. Be God’s representative and pass God’s love on to the world.
Let Christ reign in your life

Let Christ live in us and reign over our lives. Show the kingdom of God in the areas where we are. Whether in the workplace, the home, the community, or the church, lead and influence others with the wisdom and love of Christ.
Share the gospel
Bring the gospel to those we come into contact with. This can be done through verbal sharing, a life of witness, or taking part in gospel ministry.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for showing us today how to put this passage into practice in daily life. We ask You to help us stay holy, be priests of Christ, and let Christ reign in our lives and living. Give us opportunities to share the gospel, so that more people receive Your grace and salvation. We pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you experience the power of resurrection in your connection with Christ, and bring others faith, hope, and love in every corner of your life. May God’s grace and glory be with you. Amen.

t: All the Blessings Come upon You
v: It shall happen that as all the good things have come on you of which the LORD your God spoke to you, so the LORD will bring on you all the evil things, until he has destroyed you from off this good land which the LORD your God has given you,
b: This passage reminds us of the fact that blessing and calamity exist together. Sometimes we ask ourselves why, while we are going through trials, suffering, and hardship, God’s promises and blessings seem unable to come true in our lives. But let us think about this question.

The Bible tells us about the life of Joseph. When he was young, God gave him a strange dream, foretelling that in the future he would become a great leader. But his brothers, out of jealousy, sold him into Egypt as a slave. In Egypt, Joseph suffered many hardships and tests, and was even falsely accused and thrown into prison. It seemed that God’s blessing had disappeared from him.

But God still kept him in his hardship and gave him wisdom and grace. In the end Joseph became prime minister of Egypt and saved the whole country and his family from famine. God fulfilled His promise to him through Joseph’s hardship and trials.

In the same way, when we face difficulty and challenge, we may not immediately see God’s blessing shown in our lives. But it is precisely in these adversities that God shapes our character in wonderful ways and deepens our trust in Him. He makes us stronger and wiser and teaches us to walk with Him.

So when calamity comes upon us, do not forget that God’s promise does not change. He will bring blessing and good in our hardship. God has the ability to turn bad things into good, and suffering into blessing. Like Joseph, who could not see God’s plan in his hardship, yet in the end God brought his dream to pass, God will also fulfill His plan in our lives.
ah: According to the passage in Joshua 23:15, when we keep God’s commandments, Yahweh promises us all blessings, and it also tells us that if we do not keep God’s commandments, calamity will also come upon us. So how should we put this passage into practice in daily life? Here are several specific and effective ways:
a: A thankful heart

When you wake up each morning, first spend some time thanking God for the blessings He has given us, whether health, the love of family, opportunities for work, and so on. A thankful heart like this lets us treasure all we have even more.
Hold on to hope

Even when we meet difficulty or challenge, we should keep a heart full of hope as we keep God’s commandments. Trust that God will bring us solutions and strength in our hardship, and remember too that calamity will not last, and God’s blessing will come upon us and bring new hope.
Care for others

God’s commandments call us to love our neighbor as ourselves. So we should share God’s blessing with others, because through our words, deeds, and generosity they can see God’s love and grace. Whether helping those in need, encouraging others, or sharing the grace of God we have experienced, we can be channels of God and bring blessing to others.
Hold firm in faith

When we face adversity, it is very important to keep firm faith. Whether we face losing a job, health problems, difficulty in relationships, or other challenges, we should trust God’s promise and believe that He will give blessing when we need it most and lead us through the difficulty.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for all the blessings You have given us. Help us put Your word into practice in daily life and share Your love and grace with others. Give us a thankful heart, a heart full of hope, a heart that cares for others, and firm faith, so that we can rely on You in difficulty and see the blessings You have given us. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you hold firm in faith in adversity and trust God’s promise, knowing that at the right time He will fulfill His good purpose. Amen.

t: The Promised Blessing Given to Us
v: “Now, O Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
b: In this passage David expresses praise and gratitude to God, because he knows that only God is the true God, and that God has also promised to give blessing to His servant.
What is blessing? Blessing is not only abundance and success, but even more, inner peace and joy. God promises to give such blessing to us, His servants. But how can we experience such blessing?
There was a farmer who worked very hard in his fields, but his harvest was never what he had hoped for. He felt discouraged and disappointed and did not know what to do.

One day he met a wise man. The wise man told him, “Farmer, your fields need to be cultivated, and in the same way your heart needs to be cultivated. Only with a heart full of gratitude and joy can you truly experience the blessing God gives.”

When the farmer heard this, it suddenly became clear to him, and he began to change his attitude. Every morning he would spend some time thanking God for the grace and blessing in his life. He learned to see difficulties as opportunities for growth and to face the challenges of life with a thankful heart.

As time passed, the farmer began to feel the blessing God had given him. Although his harvest still had its ups and downs, his heart was full of peace and joy. He found that when he entrusted everything he had to God and trusted His promise, life became better, and he could more clearly feel God’s blessing and guidance.

Dear family, this story tells us that only with a heart of gratitude and joy can we truly experience the blessing God gives. When we entrust everything we have to God and trust His promise, God will give us peace, joy, and hope, and make our lives better.
dc:
In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you hold a heart of gratitude and joy every day and experience the blessing God gives. May God’s love fill your life and bring you faith, hope, and love. Amen.
No. 442 Soul Snack Action Guide: 2 Samuel 7:28 Now, Lord Yahweh, you are God, and your words are truth, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.

t: Blessing Will Come upon You
v: “Acquaint yourself with him now, and be at peace. By it, good will come to you.
b: This passage reminds us that knowing God is the key to receiving peace and blessing. When we build an intimate relationship with God, we can experience His peace and blessing in our lives.

A young man named Taian faced pressure and difficulty in both work and life. He felt he had lost his balance and was full of anxiety and unease. One day he met a pastor, who told Taian that knowing God is the way to true peace. From then on Taian decided to seek God, and in God’s presence he found inner stillness. He learned to trust God and let Him lead every step, and as a result his life began to become steady and full of hope. He truly experienced what the passage says: “Know God, and you will have peace.”

When we face difficulty and challenge, let us remember God’s word. He promises that blessing will come upon us. Blessing does not only mean material abundance, but the overflow of God’s grace and blessing in our lives. We can recall stories in the Bible, such as Joseph. Joseph went through much suffering in adversity, but he always held firm to God’s promise, and in the end God’s blessing came upon him abundantly.

So let us seek to know God every day and build an intimate relationship with Him. When we trust God, His peace and blessing will follow us. Whatever difficulty we face, let us rest assured that God’s grace and blessing will come upon us richly. Believe His promise, and face the challenges of life with faith and hope.
ah: This verse reminds us to know God and receive peace, because blessing will surely follow. Here are several specific ways to put this passage into practice in daily life:
a: Know God

We can come to know God more deeply by reading Scripture, praying, attending church, and fellowshipping with friends of faith. When we build an intimate relationship with God, we can experience His peace and blessing.
Keep a peaceful heart

We should learn to stay calm and at peace in the face of difficulty and pressure. Whatever challenges we meet in life, we can turn to God and trust His leading and provision, knowing that His blessing will surely come upon us.
Spread love and kindness

We can spread God’s blessing by doing good, caring for others, and passing on love and compassion. When we treat others with love, we not only let them feel God’s love, but also bring peace and blessing to ourselves.
Hold fast to faith

Whatever the circumstances, we should hold fast to faith and believe God’s promise. Sometimes we may face adversity or disappointment, but we should believe that God has a good plan in everything, and His blessing will be shown in our lives.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this beautiful passage, which reminds us to know You and receive peace, because Your blessing will surely come upon us. We ask You to help us put these action guides into practice in daily life: to build an intimate relationship with You, keep a peaceful heart, spread love and kindness, and hold fast to faith. May Your blessing keep overflowing in our lives and make us Your witnesses. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you know God’s presence today and experience His peace and blessing. May you trust God’s promise in difficulty and meet life with faith and hope. Amen.

t: Every Spiritual Blessing
v: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,
b: This passage reminds us that in Christ we can enjoy every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places. This is exciting news! Let us look deeply at the meaning of these blessings and see how they fit together with our lives.

First, “grace” is a spiritual blessing. Just as rain waters the earth, God’s grace waters the field of our hearts in our souls. Grace enables us to receive God’s forgiveness and delight and lets us build an intimate relationship with Him in life.

Second, “love” is also a spiritual blessing. God’s love flows to us selflessly and unconditionally, filling the lack and loneliness in our lives. This love also inspires us to love others and be a blessing in their lives.

There is also “hope,” which is a spiritual blessing too. When we feel despair in hardship, God’s hope gives us strength and courage. This enables us to rise above difficulty and trust God’s plan and promise.

Finally, “peace” is another spiritual blessing we have in Christ. This peace passes human understanding, and it comes from reconciliation with God and trust in Him. When we walk with Him, we can experience His peace in all kinds of circumstances and challenges and let our hearts be settled.

Dear friends, as Christians we have these abundant blessings, and these blessings can change our lives. When we meet difficulty and challenge in daily life, let us remember these blessings and face them with faith, hope, and love.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you find true joy and satisfaction in grace, love, hope, and peace. Amen.

t: That You May Inherit a Blessing
v: not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.
b: This passage reminds us that when we face malice and insult, we should respond with goodwill and pass blessing on to others. In this world we may meet unfairness and coldness, but as Christians we are called to change this situation and bring blessing to others.

A man named John was often laughed at and despised by his colleagues at work. Every day someone said unkind things to him, leaving him hurt and discouraged. But John chose to respond with goodwill. He not only did not retaliate, but chose to bless those who hurt him.

One day John noticed that a colleague often showed signs of stress and depression. He decided to take the initiative to talk with this colleague and asked whether he needed help. The colleague was surprised, because among all the mockery and insults he had received, no one had ever cared for him the way John did. In the end this colleague opened his heart and told of his troubles and pressure.

John not only listened to him but also gave support and encouragement. He encouraged the colleague to seek help and told him he was not alone. The colleague felt John’s care and love, and his stress and depression gradually eased. In the end they became friends and faced the challenges of life together.

This story tells us that even in the face of malice and insult, we can choose to respond with love and goodwill. When we pass blessing on to others, we will also reap blessing. This is not easy, but when we understand that we were called to this, we can receive strength in difficulty.
ah: 1 Peter 3:9 tells us that when others repay evil for evil and insult us, we should respond with blessing. This is truly a challenge, but we can put this passage into practice in daily life through the following ways:
a: Reflect quietly

When we are treated unfairly or insulted, do not strike back or take revenge at once, but first stop and calmly reflect on our own reaction. Ask yourself whether you can respond to the other person with love and tolerance.
Bless and pray
Learn to bless those who hurt us and to pray for them. Doing so can change our attitude, and we hope that these people too may receive God’s blessing and grace.
Coordinate and communicate
When someone treats us unfairly, we can choose to communicate in a conciliatory way. Try to understand the other person’s position and motives in order to build a better relationship.
Forgive and release
Learn to forgive those who hurt us, and release the resentment and hatred toward them. This not only frees our own hearts, but also opens up the possibility of reconciliation with them.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us this guidance in 1 Peter 3:9, which shows us how You respond to conflict between people in our daily lives. Give us wisdom and strength, so that in moments of insult and unfairness we can respond with a spirit of blessing and tolerance. Help us learn to reflect quietly, bless and pray, coordinate and communicate, and forgive and release. May our conduct show Your love and grace and be a witness that encourages others. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: may you respond to malice with goodwill and to insult with blessing. May you be the one who changes the world and brings blessing to others. Amen.

t: According to the Blessing God Has Given
v: Every man shall give as he is able, according to the LORD your God’s blessing which he has given you.
b: This passage reminds us that God gives each person a different blessing, and that we should give according to the blessing He has given down to us. Everyone has different talents and abilities, and all are equally important in God’s eyes. We should not envy others’ blessings, nor try to compare ourselves with others. Instead, we should treasure and make good use of the blessing God has given us.

In life we often fall into the trap of pursuing more, better, and higher. We may feel jealous or dissatisfied when we see what others have. But when we learn to view the blessings we have with gratitude and contentment, we will find that we already have many things to treasure.

There was a little girl named Jia’en who grew up in a poor family. Her father was a farmer who worked hard every day, but because of the weather and other factors, his harvest was small. Jia’en often saw other children in pretty clothes and with new toys, and she felt very jealous and that it was unfair.

But at a church gathering, Jia’en heard a sermon on this passage. She understood that God gives each person a different blessing, and she began to reflect on what she had. She realized that though she did not have great material wealth, she had a loving family, a healthy body, and a heart that held dreams. She began to see these precious blessings as gifts God had given her and to treat them with thanksgiving.

Jia’en showed her talent at school and became an excellent student, and through her own effort she brought change to her family. She realized that even in poor surroundings she still had the ability to change her own destiny. By giving her time and talents to help others in need, and by sharing her story with them, she encouraged them to keep going.
Dear family, let us learn with Jia’en how to look at the blessings we have with a heart of gratitude and hope, and to share them with others.
ah: Giving gifts according to the blessing God has given is one of the important practices of our daily lives as Christians. Let us think together about how to put this principle into practice:
a: Gratitude
Each morning when you rise, face the new day with a thankful heart and remember to thank God for all the blessings He has given.
Sharing
Give not only materially, but share your time, talents, and love with others.
Helping
Look for opportunities to help people in need, whether through physical or emotional support.
Sincerity
In everything you do, stay sincere with God and with people, without hypocrisy or pretense.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving us abundant blessing every day. Help us live out the spirit of gratitude, sharing, helping, and sincerity in daily life, and extend Your love and grace to others. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you: as you make good use of the blessing God has given, may you be a blessing in the lives of others. May your love and care move the world and bring people faith, hope, and love. Amen.

t: Rejoice in Your Blessing
v: You shall rejoice in all the good which the LORD your God has given to you, and to your house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner who is among you.
b: In this passage we are called to be glad and thankful for all the blessings God has given us. Whenever we think of the blessings God has given us, we should be filled with joy. Whether it is material abundance, a healthy body, the company of loved ones, or God’s grace and salvation, all these blessings come from God’s grace.

A little child looked forward every day to a delicious meal when he came home. His mother always prepared a table full of food so that he could eat and drink his fill. Whenever the child sat down at the table, his eyes would light up, full of joy and gratitude. He knew the food came from his mother’s love and care.

In the same way, we can imagine ourselves as that child, and God as our Heavenly Father. With limitless love and kindness, God prepares spiritual and material blessings for us every day. When we realize this, our hearts are filled with joy and gratitude.

Besides being joyful and thankful, this passage also reminds us to share with others the blessings we have received. The Levites and the foreigners are specially mentioned here. In the Old Testament the Levites were set apart as a special tribe to serve God, who ministered in the temple and helped people build their relationship with God. For those who play an important role in our lives, such as pastors, teachers, family, and friends, we should also be grateful to them and share our blessings with them.
ah: In daily life, we can put this passage into practice in the following ways:
a: Gratitude journal
Write down the things you are thankful for each day, recording the blessings God has given you and your family.
Share joy
Share God’s blessings with family and friends, encouraging one another and rejoicing together.
Serve others
Serve others with love and a thankful heart and pass on God’s love.
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for blessing us continually in our lives. Help us keep a thankful heart every day, and face the challenges of life with joy and thanksgiving. May we be sharers of blessing, encouraging and supporting one another. We pray in the name of the Lord Jesus. Amen.
dc: In the name of the Lord, I bless you! May you feel every day all the blessings God has given you and your household, and share this joy and gratitude with the people around you. Amen.

t: A Portion in This Life
v: from men by your hand, LORD, from men of the world, whose portion is in this life. You fill the belly of your cherished ones. Your sons have plenty, and they store up wealth for their children.
b: This passage reminds us that we live in a world full of worldly temptation and busyness. Many times we lose our spiritual direction because we pursue the blessings of this life. But Yahweh God calls to us here, hoping that we can break free from the values of the world and focus on the eternal blessing He gives us.

We often chase career success, wealth, and reputation, yet overlook what is truly important. There was a young businessman who worked day and night, constantly pursuing material satisfaction. Yet he found his soul growing emptier and emptier, lacking peace and joy within. Until one day he met a wise man, who told him a story.

There was a rich man who was very wealthy, but he kept pursuing more wealth.
